sentences.zh: __FORCETOC__狄仁傑狄仁傑，字懷英，并州太原人。

translations.literal: Di Renjie, styled Huaiying, was a man of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie, whose courtesy name was Huaiying, came from Taiyuan in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 爲兒時，門人有被害者，吏就詰，眾爭辨對，仁傑誦書不置，吏讓之，答曰：「黃卷中方與聖賢對，何暇偶俗吏語耶？」

translations.literal: When he was a child, a household member was murdered; officials came to question them. The crowd argued in defense, but Renjie recited his book without stopping. The officer rebuked him. He answered: "In my yellow scrolls I am just now facing the sages—what leisure have I to join in the talk of vulgar clerks?
translations.idiomatic: As a boy, when someone in the household was murdered and magistrates came to question the family, everyone else argued their case while Renjie kept reading without pause. When an officer scolded him, he replied: "In these pages I am in conversation with the sages—what time have I for chatter with petty clerks?

sentences.zh: 舉明經，調汴州參軍。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed adjutant at Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination and was posted as a military adjutant at Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 爲吏誣訴，黜陟使閻立本召訊，異其才，謝曰：「仲尼稱觀過知仁，君可謂滄海遺珠矣。」

translations.literal: A clerk falsely accused him. The promotion-and-demotion commissioner Yan Liben summoned and questioned him, marveled at his talent, and apologized, saying: "Confucius said that by observing faults one knows virtue—you may be called a pearl lost in the vast sea.
translations.idiomatic: After a clerk lodged a false complaint against him, the touring inspector Yan Liben summoned him for questioning, was struck by his ability, and apologized: "Confucius said one may know a man's character from his faults—you are truly a pearl cast upon the open sea.

sentences.zh: 薦授并州法曹參軍。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was appointed legal adjutant at Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On Yan's recommendation he was appointed legal adjutant in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 親在河陽，仁傑登太行山，反顧，見白雲孤飛，謂左右曰：「吾親舍其下。」

translations.literal: His parents were at Heyang. Renjie climbed Mount Taihang, looked back, and saw a lone white cloud drifting. He said to those beside him: "My parents dwell beneath it.
translations.idiomatic: While his parents were living at Heyang, Renjie climbed the Taihang range, turned to look back, and saw a solitary white cloud drifting by. He told his attendants: "My parents are staying beneath that cloud.

sentences.zh: 瞻悵久之，雲移乃得去。

translations.literal: He gazed long in melancholy longing; only when the cloud had moved on could he depart.
translations.idiomatic: He stood gazing after it for a long while in sorrowful longing, and only when the cloud had drifted away could he bring himself to leave.

sentences.zh: 同府參軍鄭崇質母老且疾，當使絶域。

translations.literal: A fellow adjutant in the prefecture, Zheng Chongzhi, had a mother who was old and ill, yet was to be sent on mission to a distant frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chongzhi, another adjutant in the prefecture, had an aged, ailing mother yet had been ordered on a mission to a distant border region.

sentences.zh: 仁傑謂曰：「君可貽親萬里憂乎？」

translations.literal: Renjie said to him: "Can you leave your parents a care ten thousand li away?
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said to him: "Would you lay a grief ten thousand li away upon your parents?

sentences.zh: 詣長史藺仁基請代行。

translations.literal: He went to the chief secretary Lan Renji and asked to go in his place.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to the chief secretary Lan Renji and asked to take Zheng's place on the mission.

sentences.zh: 仁基咨美其誼，時方與司馬李孝廉不平，相敕曰：「吾等可少愧矣！」

translations.literal: Renji praised his sense of duty. At the time he was at odds with the marshal Li Xiaolian; they admonished each other, saying: "We should be somewhat ashamed!
translations.idiomatic: Renji commended his filial devotion. At the time he was estranged from the marshal Li Xiaolian; the two admonished each other, saying: "We ought to feel a little ashamed of ourselves!

sentences.zh: 則相待如初，毎曰：「狄公之賢，北斗以南，一人而已。」

translations.literal: From then on they treated each other as before, and Li always said: "Among the worthy of Lord Di, there is but one man south of the Pole Star."
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they treated each other as before, and Li would often say: "For worthiness like Lord Di's, there is only one man this side of the Southern Dipper."

sentences.zh: 稍遷大理丞，歳中斷久獄萬七千人，時稱平恕。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review; within a year he resolved more than seventeen thousand long-stagnant cases. The age praised him as fair and lenient.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and within a year cleared more than seventeen thousand long-pending cases, winning renown for fairness and clemency.

sentences.zh: 左威衞大將軍權善才、右監門中郎將範懷義坐誤斧昭陵柏，罪當免，高宗詔誅之。

translations.literal: Left Majestic Guard General Quan Shancai and Right Supervisor of the Palace Gate Central Companion Fan Huaiyi were convicted of mistakenly felling a cypress at the Zhao Mausoleum; by law they should have been pardoned, but Emperor Gaozong ordered their execution.
translations.idiomatic: Left Majestic Guard General Quan Shancai and Right Supervisor of the Palace Gate Central Companion Fan Huaiyi were found guilty of accidentally cutting down a cypress at the Zhao Mausoleum—a crime punishable by dismissal—yet Emperor Gaozong ordered them put to death.

sentences.zh: 仁傑奏不應死，帝怒曰：「是使我爲不孝子，必殺之。」

translations.literal: Renjie memorialized that they should not die. The emperor was angry and said: "This makes me an unfilial son—I must kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie submitted that they did not deserve death. The emperor flew into a rage: "This would make me an unfilial son—I insist on executing them.

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「漢有盜高廟玉環，文帝欲當之族，張釋之廷諍曰：『假令取長陵一抔土，何以加其法？』

translations.literal: Renjie said: "In Han times thieves stole a jade ring from the imperial temple. Emperor Wen wished to punish their entire clan. Zhang Shizhi argued in court: 'Suppose one took a handful of earth from Changling—how would you increase their penalty?
translations.idiomatic: Renjie replied: "Under the Han, men stole a jade ring from the imperial temple. Emperor Wen meant to wipe out their whole clan, but Zhang Shizhi remonstrated in open court: 'If someone took a handful of soil from Chang Mausoleum, how would you make the penalty heavier?

sentences.zh: 於是罪止棄市。

translations.literal: Thus the crime was limited to public execution.
translations.idiomatic: The punishment was therefore limited to public execution.

sentences.zh: 陛下之法在象魏，固有差等。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's laws are posted at the elephant-gate tower; they certainly have gradations.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's laws are displayed at the elephant-gate tower and plainly set out gradations of punishment.

sentences.zh: 犯不至死而致之死，何哉？

translations.literal: If the offence does not reach death yet you cause death, why?
translations.idiomatic: When the offence does not warrant death, why bring death upon the offenders?

sentences.zh: 今誤伐一柏，殺二臣，後世謂陛下爲何如主？」

translations.literal: Now for mistakenly cutting down one cypress you kill two ministers—what will posterity call your Majesty as a ruler?"
translations.idiomatic: Now, for mistakenly felling one cypress, you would kill two ministers—what kind of ruler will posterity call your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 帝意解，遂免死。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind relented and they were spared death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger eased, and the two men were spared.

sentences.zh: 數日，授侍御史。

translations.literal: Several days later he was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 左司郎中王本立怙寵自肆，仁傑劾奏其惡，有詔原之。

translations.literal: Left Department Director Wang Benli relied on favor and acted wantonly. Renjie impeached and reported his wickedness; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Benli of the Left Department, trusting in imperial favor, behaved with arrogant license. Renjie impeached him for misconduct, but an edict pardoned Wang.

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「朝廷借乏賢，如本立者不鮮。

translations.literal: Renjie said: "The court is said to lack worthy men, yet men like Benli are not few.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said: "The court is said to lack talent, yet men like Benli are hardly rare.

sentences.zh: 陛下惜有罪，虧成法，奈何？

translations.literal: Your Majesty pities the guilty and impairs the established law—how can this be?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty would spare the guilty and undermine settled law—how can that be justified?

sentences.zh: 臣願先斥，爲群臣戒。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to be dismissed first, as a warning to the multitude of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to be dismissed first, as a warning to the other officials.

sentences.zh: 本立抵罪。

translations.literal: Benli was punished for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Benli was duly punished.

sentences.zh: 繇是朝廷肅然。

translations.literal: From this the court became solemn and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the court grew markedly more disciplined.

sentences.zh: 使岐州，亡卒數百剽行人，道不通。

translations.literal: Sent to Qizhou: several hundred deserters plundered travelers and the roads were impassable.
translations.idiomatic: On assignment to Qizhou, he found several hundred deserters robbing travelers so that the roads were unsafe.

sentences.zh: 官捕系盜黨窮訊，而余曹紛紛不能制。

translations.literal: Officials arrested and bound the bandit faction and interrogated them exhaustively, yet the remaining gangs swarmed about and could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Officials had arrested the ringleaders and interrogated them harshly, yet the remaining bands still ran riot beyond control.

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「是其計窮，且爲患。」

translations.literal: Renjie said: "Their stratagems are exhausted and they will yet become a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said: "They are at their wits' end and will only grow more dangerous.

sentences.zh: 乃明開首原格，出繫者，稟而縱之，使相曉，皆自縛歸。

translations.literal: He then clearly opened the amnesty for those who came forward first, released the bound prisoners, reported and set them free, and had them inform one another; all came back bound of their own accord.
translations.idiomatic: He publicly announced an amnesty for those who surrendered first, released the prisoners, and sent them out to spread word of it; every man came back and bound himself of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 帝歎其達權宜。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his grasp of expedient measures.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his grasp of practical expedients.

sentences.zh: 遷度支郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be director of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 帝幸汾陽宮，爲知頓使。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Fenyang Palace, Renjie served as commissioner for provisioning.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Fenyang Palace, Renjie served as provisioning commissioner.

sentences.zh: 并州長史李沖玄以道出妒女祠，俗言盛服過者，致風雷之變，更發卒數萬改馳道。

translations.literal: Bingzhou chief secretary Li Chongxuan, because the road passed the Jealous Woman Shrine—popular lore held that those in splendid dress who passed it brought wind and thunder—again mobilized tens of thousands of laborers to reroute the imperial highway.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhou chief secretary Li Chongxuan, because the route passed the Jealous Woman Shrine—where folk belief held that travelers in fine dress would stir wind and thunder—drafted tens of thousands of men to reroute the imperial highway.

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「天子之行，風伯清塵，雨師灑道，何妒女避邪？」

translations.literal: Renjie said: "On the Son of Heaven's progress, the Wind Lord clears the dust and the Rain Master sprinkles the road—why avoid an evil jealous woman?
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said: "When the Son of Heaven travels, the Wind Lord clears the dust and the Rain Master wets the road—why should he shun some jealous woman's shrine?

sentences.zh: 止其役。

translations.literal: He stopped the labor.
translations.idiomatic: He halted the project.

sentences.zh: 帝壯之，曰：「真丈夫哉！」

translations.literal: The emperor admired him and said: "A true man indeed!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed and exclaimed: "What a true man!

sentences.zh: 出爲甯州刺史，撫和戎落，得其歡心，郡人勒碑以頌。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Ningzhou, soothed and harmonized the frontier tribes, won their hearts, and the people of the commandery carved a stele in praise.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Ningzhou, won over the frontier tribes by gentle rule, and earned their goodwill; the people of the prefecture erected a stele in his honor.

sentences.zh: 入拜冬官侍郎、持節江南巡撫使。

translations.literal: He entered court as vice minister of the Works Department and commissioner with the staff of authority to tour and pacify the south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as vice minister of the Works Department and imperial commissioner to tour and pacify the Jiangnan region.

sentences.zh: 呉、楚俗多淫祠，仁傑一禁止，凡毀千七百房，止留夏禹、呉太伯、季劄、伍員四祠而已。

translations.literal: Wu and Chu custom had many improper shrines; Renjie banned them all at once, destroying in all seventeen hundred halls, and left only four shrines—to Yu of Xia, Taibo of Wu, Jizha, and Wu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Chu were rife with improper shrines; Renjie suppressed them in one sweep, demolishing seventeen hundred halls in all and sparing only four—to Yu of Xia, Taibo of Wu, Jizha, and Wu Zixu.

sentences.zh: 轉文昌右丞，出豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right vice director of the Secretariat and sent out as prefect of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right vice director of the Secretariat and appointed prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時越王兵敗，支党餘二千人論死。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Yue's army had been defeated; more than two thousand of his partisans remained, sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yue's rebellion had just been crushed, and more than two thousand of his followers still faced execution.

sentences.zh: 仁傑釋其械，密疏曰：「臣欲有所陳，似爲逆人申理；

translations.literal: Renjie released their fetters and submitted a secret memorial: "Your servant wishes to speak out—it may seem as though I am pleading the cause of rebels;
translations.idiomatic: Renjie had their shackles removed and sent a secret memorial: "I wish to speak frankly, though it may look as if I am pleading for rebels;

sentences.zh: 不言，且累陛下欽恤意。

translations.literal: yet if I do not speak, I will burden your Majesty's intent of compassionate forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: yet if I stay silent, I will betray your Majesty's own intent of merciful forbearance.

sentences.zh: 表成復毀，自不能定。

translations.literal: When the memorial was finished I destroyed it again; I myself could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: I drafted the memorial and tore it up again, unable to settle my own mind.

sentences.zh: 然此皆非本惡，詿誤至此。」

translations.literal: Yet these men were not evil by nature; they were misled and blundered to this point.
translations.idiomatic: These men were not wicked by nature; they were led astray and stumbled into crime.

sentences.zh: 有詔悉謫戍邊。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all of them banished to garrison the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: An edict banished them all to frontier garrison duty instead.

sentences.zh: 囚出寧州，父老迎勞曰：「狄使君活汝耶！」

translations.literal: As the prisoners left Ningzhou, the elders came out to welcome and comfort them, saying: "Did Commissioner Di save your lives?
translations.idiomatic: As the prisoners passed through Ningzhou, the elders came out to greet them, crying: "Did Commissioner Di save you?

sentences.zh: 因相與哭碑下。

translations.literal: Thereupon together they wept beneath the stele.
translations.idiomatic: They wept together beneath his stele.

sentences.zh: 囚齋三日乃去。

translations.literal: The prisoners fasted three days before departing.
translations.idiomatic: The prisoners observed three days of fasting before they left.

sentences.zh: 至流所，亦爲立碑。

translations.literal: When they reached their place of exile, they also erected a stele for him.
translations.idiomatic: At their place of exile they erected another stele in his honor.

sentences.zh: 初，宰相張光輔討越王。

translations.literal: Earlier, the chief minister Zhang Guangfu had campaigned against the Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, chief minister Zhang Guangfu had led the campaign against the Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 軍中恃功，多暴索，仁傑拒之。

translations.literal: In the army many relied on their merit and made violent demands; Renjie refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Many in the army, trusting in their merit, made violent demands; Renjie turned them down.

sentences.zh: 光輔怒曰：「州將輕元帥邪？」

translations.literal: Guangfu angrily said: "Does the prefect slight the commander-in-chief?
translations.idiomatic: Guangfu snapped: "Does a prefect dare slight the commander-in-chief?

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「亂河南者一越王，公董士三十萬以平亂，縱使暴橫，使無辜之人鹹墜塗炭，是一越王死，百越王生也。

translations.literal: Renjie said: "The one who disturbed Henan was a single Prince of Yue. You marshal three hundred thousand men to quell disorder—yet even if you act with violent arrogance and let innocent people all fall into ruin, it is one Prince of Yue dead and a hundred Princes of Yue born.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie replied: "Only one Prince of Yue stirred trouble in Henan. You command three hundred thousand troops to put down rebellion—yet if you let your men run wild and innocent people suffer ruin, you will kill one Prince of Yue and breed a hundred more.

sentences.zh: 且王師之至，民歸順以萬計，自縋而下，四面成蹊。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the royal army arrived, the people submitted in tens of thousands, lowering themselves by rope; on all sides paths were worn.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army arrived, tens of thousands of people came over in submission, lowering themselves down by rope until paths were worn on every side.

sentences.zh: 奈何縱邀賞之人殺降以爲功，冤痛徹天？

translations.literal: How can you indulge men who seek rewards to kill those who surrender and call it merit, until grievous wrongs pierce heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Why let men hungry for reward slaughter those who surrender and call it achievement, until the people's anguish reaches heaven itself?

sentences.zh: 如得上方斬馬劍加君頸，雖死不恨！」

translations.literal: If I could have the imperial executioner's sword placed at your neck, I would die without regret!"
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor's executioner's sword could be laid to your neck, I would die content!"

sentences.zh: 光輔還，奏仁傑不遜，左授復州刺史。

translations.literal: Guangfu returned and memorialized that Renjie was insubordinate; Renjie was demoted to the left and appointed prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangfu returned to court he reported Renjie for insubordination, and Renjie was demoted to prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 徙洛州司馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be marshal of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to serve as marshal of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 天授二年，以地官侍郎同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshou he was made vice minister of the Land Department and associate director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, with the rank of Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianshou (691) he was appointed vice minister of the Land Department and Grand Councillor of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.

sentences.zh: 武后謂曰：「卿在汝南有善政，然有譖卿者，欲知之乎？」

translations.literal: Empress Wu said to him: "You had good government at Runan, yet there are those who slander you—do you wish to know who they are?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu said to him: "You governed Runan well, yet someone has been slandering you—would you like to know who?

sentences.zh: 謝曰：「陛下以爲過，臣當改之；

translations.literal: He declined, saying: "If your Majesty thinks it a fault, your servant will reform it;
translations.idiomatic: He declined: "If Your Majesty believes I have erred, I shall reform;

sentences.zh: 以爲無過，臣之幸也。

translations.literal: if your Majesty thinks there is no fault, it is your servant's good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: if Your Majesty believes I have not erred, that is my good fortune.

sentences.zh: 譖者乃不願知。」

translations.literal: As for the slanderers, I do not wish to know them."
translations.idiomatic: As for who slandered me, I would rather not know."

sentences.zh: 后歎其長者。

translations.literal: The empress sighed at his magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: The empress sighed in admiration of his forbearance.

sentences.zh: 時太學生謁急，后亦報可。

translations.literal: At the time an Imperial University student requested urgent leave; the empress also approved it.
translations.idiomatic: When an Imperial University student petitioned for urgent leave, the empress had already approved it.

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「人君惟生殺柄不以假人，至簿書期會，宜責有司。

translations.literal: Renjie said: "The ruler's authority over life and death alone is not to be lent to others; as for documents, schedules, and deadlines, the responsible offices should be charged.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said: "A ruler should reserve the power of life and death and not delegate it; routine paperwork and deadlines ought to be left to the proper offices.

sentences.zh: 尚書省決事，左、右丞不句杖，左、右丞相不判徒，況天子乎？

translations.literal: In the Department of State Affairs, the left and right assistant directors do not pass on cases of beating; the left and right chancellors do not judge exile—how much less the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: In the Department of State Affairs, the left and right assistant directors do not sign off on flogging cases, and the left and right chancellors do not rule on exile—how much less should the Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 學徒取告，丞、簿職耳，若爲報可，則胄子數千，凡幾詔耶？

translations.literal: A student's request for leave is the duty of an assistant director or registrar—if Your Majesty approves each one, with several thousand students, how many edicts would there be?
translations.idiomatic: A student's leave petition is clerks' work; if Your Majesty approves each one personally, with thousands of students how many edicts would that require?

sentences.zh: 爲定令示之而已。」

translations.literal: Simply establish a regulation and show it to them.
translations.idiomatic: Simply issue a fixed regulation and let them follow it.

sentences.zh: 后納其言。

translations.literal: The empress accepted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The empress took his advice.

sentences.zh: 會爲來俊臣所構，捕送制獄。

translations.literal: He happened to be framed by Lai Junchen, was arrested and sent to the special prison.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon framed by Lai Junchen, arrested, and sent to the special prison.

sentences.zh: 于時，訊反者一問即臣，聽減死。

translations.literal: At that time, those interrogated for rebellion confessed at the first question and were allowed commuted death.
translations.idiomatic: At that time anyone interrogated for treason confessed at the first question and was allowed to plead for a reduced sentence.

sentences.zh: 俊臣引仁傑置對，答曰：「有周革命，我乃唐臣，反固實。」

translations.literal: Junchen brought Renjie forth for confrontation; he answered: "The Zhou has undergone its revolution; I am still a Tang subject—rebellion is indeed the fact.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen brought Renjie out for questioning; he answered: "The Zhou has replaced the dynasty; I remain a subject of Tang—treason is indeed the truth.

sentences.zh: 俊臣乃挺系。

translations.literal: Junchen then had him bound with cangue and chains.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen then had him shackled in the cangue.

sentences.zh: 其屬王德壽以情謂曰：「我意求少遷，公爲我引楊執柔爲黨，公且免死。」

translations.literal: His subordinate Wang Deshou spoke to him privately, saying: "I wish for a small promotion—if you will name Yang Zhirou as my accomplice for me, you may yet escape death.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinate Wang Deshou spoke to him in confidence: "I am angling for a small promotion—if you will name Yang Zhirou as my accomplice, you may yet escape death.

sentences.zh: 仁傑歎曰；

translations.literal: Renjie sighed and said:
translations.idiomatic: Renjie sighed and said:

sentences.zh: 「皇天后土，使仁傑爲此乎！」

translations.literal: "Heaven above and earth below—would you have Renjie do this!
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven and earth—would you have Renjie do such a thing!

sentences.zh: 即以首觸柱，血流沫面。

translations.literal: He immediately struck his head against a pillar; blood flowed and foamed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately dashed his head against a pillar until blood streamed and foamed across his face.

sentences.zh: 德壽懼而謝。

translations.literal: Deshou was afraid and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Deshou was frightened and apologized.

sentences.zh: 守者浸弛，即丐筆書帛，置褚衣中，好謂吏曰；

translations.literal: The guards gradually relaxed their vigil; he begged for brush and silk, wrote on cloth, placed it in his padded garment, and spoke kindly to the clerk:
translations.idiomatic: As the guards grew lax, he begged for brush and cloth, wrote a message, hid it in his padded coat, and said pleasantly to a clerk:

sentences.zh: 「方暑，請付家徹絮。」

translations.literal: "It is hot—please have my family change my cotton padding.
translations.idiomatic: "The weather is hot—please ask my family to change my cotton padding.

sentences.zh: 仁傑子光遠得書上變，后遣使案視。

translations.literal: Renjie's son Guangyuan obtained the letter and submitted an urgent report; the empress sent an envoy to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie's son Guangyuan got hold of the letter and submitted an urgent appeal; the empress sent an envoy to investigate.

sentences.zh: 俊臣命仁傑冠帶見使者，私令德壽作謝死表，附使以聞。

translations.literal: Junchen ordered Renjie to don cap and belt to meet the envoy, and secretly had Deshou draft a memorial thanking for death, to be sent with the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Junchen ordered Renjie to dress in cap and belt to meet the envoy and secretly had Deshou draft a memorial accepting death, to be sent along with the envoy's report.

sentences.zh: 后乃召見仁傑，謂曰：「承反何耶？」

translations.literal: The empress then summoned Renjie and said: "You admit rebellion—what is this?
translations.idiomatic: The empress then summoned Renjie and asked: "You confessed treason—what was that about?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「不承反，死笞掠矣。」

translations.literal: He answered: "If I had not admitted rebellion, I would have died under the flogging."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "If I had not confessed treason, I would have been beaten to death."

sentences.zh: 示其表，曰：「無之。」

translations.literal: She showed him the memorial; he said: "There was none."
translations.idiomatic: She showed him the memorial; he said: "I wrote no such thing."

sentences.zh: 后知代署，因免死。

translations.literal: The empress knew it had been written in his place and therefore spared his life.
translations.idiomatic: The empress realized someone else had written it and spared his life.

sentences.zh: 武承嗣屢請誅之，后曰：「命已行，不可返。」

translations.literal: Wu Chengsi repeatedly asked that he be executed; the empress said: "The decree has already been carried out—it cannot be reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengsi repeatedly pressed for his execution; the empress said: "The order has already gone forth—it cannot be taken back.

sentences.zh: 時同被誣者鳳閣侍郎任知古等七族悉得貸。

translations.literal: At the time those falsely accused with him—Phoenix Pavilion vice director Ren Zhigu and seven clans in all—were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, all seven clans implicated with him, including Phoenix Pavilion vice director Ren Zhigu, were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 御史霍獻可以首叩殿陛苦爭，欲必殺仁傑等，乃貶仁傑彭澤令，邑人爲置生祠。

translations.literal: Censor Huo Xianyi knocked his head on the palace steps in bitter argument, wishing to have Renjie and the others surely killed; Renjie was therefore demoted to magistrate of Pengze, and the people of the district erected a living shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Huo Xianyi battered his head on the palace steps arguing that Renjie and the others must die; Renjie was demoted to magistrate of Pengze instead, and the people of the district erected a living shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 萬歳通天中，契丹陷冀州，河北震動，擢仁傑爲魏州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian era the Khitans took Jizhou; Hebei was shaken; Renjie was promoted to prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wansui Tongtian period the Khitans captured Jizhou and threw Hebei into alarm; Renjie was promoted to prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 前刺史懼賊至，驅民保城，修守具。

translations.literal: The previous prefect, fearing the bandits' arrival, drove the people to shelter in the city and repaired defensive equipment.
translations.idiomatic: The previous prefect, fearing the enemy's approach, had driven the people into the city and rushed repairs to its defenses.

sentences.zh: 仁傑至，曰：「賊在遠，何自疲民？

translations.literal: When Renjie arrived he said: "The bandits are far away—why weary the people of your own accord?
translations.idiomatic: When Renjie arrived he said: "The enemy is still far off—why exhaust the people before there is any need?

sentences.zh: 萬一虜來，吾自辦之，何預若輩？」

translations.literal: If by chance the barbarians come, I will handle it myself—what concern is it of you people?
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy should come after all, I will deal with it myself—what business is that of yours?

sentences.zh: 悉縱就田。

translations.literal: He released them all to return to their fields.
translations.idiomatic: He sent them all back to their fields.

sentences.zh: 虜聞，亦引去，民愛仰之，復爲立祠。

translations.literal: When the barbarians heard of it, they too withdrew. The people loved and looked up to him, and again erected a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans heard of this, they withdrew as well. The people loved and revered him, and once again built a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 俄轉幽州都督，賜紫袍、龜帶，后自製金字十二於袍，以旌其忠。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be Military Governor of Youzhou. He was granted a purple robe and a turtle belt. The Empress herself inscribed twelve gold characters on the robe to honor his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to serve as Military Governor of Youzhou and was granted a purple robe and a turtle belt. The Empress herself wrote twelve gold characters on the robe to commend his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 召拜鸞臺侍郎，復同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Luantai Secretariat, and again served concurrently as Grand Councilor of the Fengge and Luantai Secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed Vice Director of the Luantai Secretariat, resuming his concurrent post as Grand Councilor of the Fengge and Luantai Secretariats.

sentences.zh: 時發兵戍疏勒四鎮，百姓怨苦。

translations.literal: At the time troops were being dispatched to garrison the Four Garrisons centered on Shule, and the common people groaned under the burden.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court was sending troops to garrison the Four Garrisons of Anxi, centered on Shule, and the people were bitter with resentment.

sentences.zh: 仁傑諫曰：

translations.literal: Renjie admonished the throne, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Renjie memorialized the throne, saying:

sentences.zh: 天生四夷，皆在先王封域之外。

translations.literal: Heaven gave birth to the four barbarian peoples, all of whom lie beyond the domains that the ancient kings enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven created the four barbarian peoples, and all of them dwell beyond the domains the ancient kings once enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 東距滄海，西隔流沙，北橫大漠，南阻五嶺，天所以限中外也。

translations.literal: To the east they are bounded by the blue sea, to the west cut off by drifting sands, to the north stretched across by the great desert, and to the south blocked by the Five Ranges—these are Heaven's barriers between the Middle Kingdom and the outer world.
translations.idiomatic: To the east lies the blue sea, to the west drifting sands, to the north the great desert, and to the south the Five Ranges—Heaven's own boundaries between the Middle Kingdom and the outer world.

sentences.zh: 自典籍所紀，聲教所暨，三代不能至者，國家既已兼之。

translations.literal: As recorded in the canonical texts and as far as civilizing influence has reached, territories that the Three Dynasties could not attain, our state has already embraced them all.
translations.idiomatic: From what the canonical texts record and from how far civilizing influence has reached, lands the Three Dynasties never attained, our dynasty has already brought under its sway.

sentences.zh: 詩人矜薄伐於太原，化行於江、漢，前代之遐裔，而我之域中，過夏、商遠矣。

translations.literal: The poets boast of a slight expedition to Taiyuan, and civilizing influence extended to the Yangtze and Han rivers—yet the remote edges of earlier dynasties are now within our realm, far surpassing the Xia and Shang.
translations.idiomatic: The poets once boasted of a modest campaign as far as Taiyuan and of civilization reaching the Yangtze and Han rivers—yet the distant frontiers of earlier dynasties are now within our own domain, far beyond what the Xia and Shang ever achieved.

sentences.zh: 今乃用武荒外，邀功絶域，竭府庫之實，以爭磽確不毛之地，得其人不足以增賦，獲其土不可以耕織。

translations.literal: Now we employ arms in the outer wastes, seeking merit in the farthest lands, exhausting the treasury's reserves to contest barren, infertile ground—gaining its people would not suffice to increase tax revenue, and seizing its soil would not serve for plowing and weaving.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now we employ arms in the outer wastes, seeking glory in the farthest reaches, draining the treasury to fight over barren, unproductive land—its people would not add enough to the tax rolls, and its soil would not sustain farming or weaving.

sentences.zh: 苟求冠帶遠夷，不務固本安人，此秦皇、漢武之所行也。

translations.literal: If one merely seeks to bring distant barbarians under the cap and sash, and does not devote oneself to securing the foundation and settling the people, this is what the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han did.
translations.idiomatic: If one seeks only to bring distant barbarians into the fold of civilization and does not devote oneself to securing the foundations and settling the people, one is following the path of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「與覆車同軌者未嘗安。」

translations.literal: The tradition says: "Those who follow the same track as an overturned cart have never found safety.
translations.idiomatic: The tradition says: "Those who follow the same track as an overturned cart have never found safety.

sentences.zh: 此言雖小，可以喻大。

translations.literal: Though this saying is small, it can illustrate a great matter.
translations.idiomatic: Though this saying is small, it can illustrate a great matter.

sentences.zh: 臣伏見國家師旅歳出，調度之費狃以浸廣，右戍四鎮，左屯安東，杼軸空匱，轉輸不絶，行役既久，怨曠者多。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly observes that the state's armies go forth year after year, and the costs of provisioning grow ever wider. We garrison the Four Garrisons on the right and station troops in Andong on the left. The looms are emptied and the stores exhausted; transport never ceases. Service has dragged on so long that the resentful and the widowed are many.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant humbly observes that the state's armies march out year after year, and provisioning costs grow ever larger. We garrison the Four Garrisons in the west and station troops in Andong in the east. Household looms stand idle and storehouses run empty; transport never stops. Service has dragged on so long that widows and the resentful are everywhere.

sentences.zh: 上不是恤，則政不行；

translations.literal: If the ruler above does not attend to this with concern, then policy cannot be carried out;
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler above does not attend to this with concern, policy cannot be carried out;

sentences.zh: 政不行，則害氣作；

translations.literal: if policy is not carried out, then harmful influences arise;
translations.idiomatic: if policy fails, harmful forces arise;

sentences.zh: 害氣作，則蟲螟生，水旱起矣。

translations.literal: when harmful influences arise, then locusts and caterpillars are born, and floods and droughts follow.
translations.idiomatic: when harmful forces arise, pests multiply and floods and droughts follow.

sentences.zh: 方今關東薦饑，蜀漢流亡，江、淮而南，賦斂不息。

translations.literal: At present famine recurs in the lands east of the Pass, refugees flee from Shu and Han, and south of the Yangtze and Huai, tax levies never cease.
translations.idiomatic: At present famine recurs east of the Pass, refugees stream from Shu and Han, and south of the Yangtze and Huai, tax levies never cease.

sentences.zh: 人不復本，則相率爲盜，本根一搖，憂患非淺。

translations.literal: When people cannot return to their livelihoods, they will band together as bandits. Once the root is shaken, the troubles will not be slight.
translations.idiomatic: When people cannot return to their livelihoods, they band together as bandits. Once the root is shaken, the troubles will run deep.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，皆貪功方外，耗竭中國也。

translations.literal: The reason for all this is the greed for merit beyond the borders, which exhausts the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: The reason for all this is the greed for glory beyond the borders, which drains the heartland dry.

sentences.zh: 昔漢元帝納賈捐之之謀而罷珠崖，宣帝用魏相之策而棄車師田。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Yuan of Han accepted Jia Juanzhi's plan and abandoned Zhuya; Emperor Xuan employed Wei Xiang's strategy and gave up the fields of Cheshi.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Emperor Yuan of Han accepted Jia Juanzhi's counsel and abandoned Zhuya, and Emperor Xuan adopted Wei Xiang's strategy and gave up the fields of Cheshi.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，克平九姓，冊拜李思摩爲可汗，使統諸部，夷狄叛則伐，降則撫，得推亡固存之義，無遠戍勞人之役。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, after the Nine Surnamed tribes were pacified, Li Simo was enfeoffed as khan and made to command the various tribes. When the barbarians rebelled they were attacked; when they submitted they were comforted. This embodied the principle of supporting the perishing and preserving the surviving, without the burden of distant garrison service.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era, after the Nine Surnamed tribes were pacified, Li Simo was enfeoffed as khan to command the various tribes. When the barbarians rebelled they were attacked; when they submitted they were comforted. This embodied the principle of supporting the perishing and preserving the surviving, without the burden of distant garrison service.

sentences.zh: 今阿史那斛瑟羅，皆陰山貴種，代雄沙漠，若委之四鎮，以統諸蕃，建爲可汗，遣禦寇患，則國家有繼絶之美，無轉輸之苦。

translations.literal: Now Ashina Huseluo is of the noble stock of the Yin Mountains and has been a desert power for generations. If he were entrusted with the Four Garrisons to command the various tribes, established as khan, and charged with repelling invaders, then the state would gain the merit of continuing a broken line and be spared the hardship of transport.
translations.idiomatic: Now Ashina Huseluo is of the noble stock of the Yin Mountains and has been a desert power for generations. If he were entrusted with the Four Garrisons to command the various tribes, established as khan, and charged with repelling invaders, the state would gain the merit of continuing a broken line and be spared the hardship of transport.

sentences.zh: 損四鎮，肥中國，罷安東，實遼西，省軍費於遠方，並甲兵於要塞，恒、代之鎮重，而邊州之備豐矣。

translations.literal: Reduce the Four Garrisons and enrich the Middle Kingdom; abolish Andong and strengthen Liaoxi; save military expenses in distant lands and concentrate armor and troops at the strongholds—the defenses of Heng and Dai would be made weighty, and the border prefectures would be well prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce the Four Garrisons and strengthen the heartland; abolish Andong and fortify Liaoxi; save military expenses in distant lands and concentrate armor and troops at the strongholds—the defenses of Heng and Dai would be made weighty, and the border prefectures would be well prepared.

sentences.zh: 且王者外甯，容有內危。

translations.literal: Moreover, when a true king brings peace to the outer world, he may yet harbor inner peril.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when a true king brings peace to the outer world, he may yet harbor danger within.

sentences.zh: 陛下姑敕邊兵謹守備，以逸待勞，則戰士力倍；

translations.literal: Your Majesty should for the time being order the border troops to guard their defenses carefully. If they wait at ease for the weary enemy, the warriors' strength will be doubled;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should for the time being order the border troops to hold their defenses carefully. If they wait at ease for the weary enemy, the warriors' strength will be doubled;

sentences.zh: 以主禦客，則我得其便；

translations.literal: if the host meets the guest, then we gain the advantage;
translations.idiomatic: if the defender meets the invader, we gain the advantage;

sentences.zh: 堅壁清野，寇無所得。

translations.literal: with strong walls and cleared fields, the invaders will gain nothing.
translations.idiomatic: With strong walls and cleared fields, the invaders will gain nothing.

sentences.zh: 自然深入有顛躓之慮，淺入無虜獲之益。

translations.literal: Naturally, if they penetrate deeply they will fear stumbling; if they penetrate shallowly they will gain no booty.
translations.idiomatic: Naturally, if they penetrate deeply they will fear stumbling; if they penetrate shallowly they will gain no booty.

sentences.zh: 不數年，二虜不討而服矣。

translations.literal: Within a few years, the two barbarian peoples will submit without being chastised.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years, the two barbarian peoples will submit without being chastised.

sentences.zh: 又請廢安東，復高姓爲君長，省江南轉餉以息民，不見納。

translations.literal: He also requested the abolition of Andong, the restoration of the Gao clan as local rulers, and the saving of grain transport from the south of the Yangtze to give the people rest. This was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested the abolition of Andong, the restoration of the Gao clan as local rulers, and relief from grain transport from south of the Yangtze to give the people rest. The proposal was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 張易之嘗從容問自安計，仁傑曰：「惟勸迎廬陵王可以免禍。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yizhi once casually asked him for a plan to ensure his own safety. Renjie said: "Only by advising the Empress to welcome back the Prince of Luling can one avoid disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yizhi once casually asked him for a plan to ensure his own safety. Renjie said: "Only by advising the Empress to welcome back the Prince of Luling can one avoid disaster.

sentences.zh: 會后欲以武三思爲太子，以問宰相，眾莫敢對。

translations.literal: At that time the Empress wished to make Wu Sansi crown prince and asked the chief ministers. None dared reply.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Empress wished to make Wu Sansi crown prince and asked the chief ministers. None dared reply.

sentences.zh: 仁傑曰：「臣觀天人未厭唐德。

translations.literal: Renjie said: "Your servant observes that Heaven and the people have not yet grown weary of the virtue of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie said: "Your servant observes that Heaven and the people have not yet grown weary of the virtue of Tang.

sentences.zh: 比匈奴犯邊，陛下使梁王三思募勇士於市，逾月不及千人。

translations.literal: When the Xiongnu recently violated the border, Your Majesty had Prince of Liang Sansi recruit brave men in the markets, yet in more than a month he did not reach a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks recently violated the border, Your Majesty had Prince of Liang Sansi recruit brave men in the markets, yet in more than a month he did not reach a thousand.

sentences.zh: 廬陵王代之，不浹日，輒五萬。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Luling replaced him, in less than a day there were fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Luling replaced him, in less than a day there were fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 今欲繼統，非廬陵王莫可。」

translations.literal: If you now wish to continue the succession, none but the Prince of Luling will do.
translations.idiomatic: If you now wish to continue the succession, none but the Prince of Luling will do.

sentences.zh: 后怒，罷議。

translations.literal: The Empress was angry and dismissed the discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress was angry and dismissed the discussion.

sentences.zh: 久之，召謂曰：「朕數夢雙陸不勝，何也？」

translations.literal: After some time she summoned him and said: "I repeatedly dream that I lose at backgammon—why is this?
translations.idiomatic: After some time she summoned him and said: "I repeatedly dream that I lose at backgammon—why is this?

sentences.zh: 於是，仁傑與王方慶俱在，二人同辭對曰：「雙陸不勝，無子也。

translations.literal: At that time Renjie and Wang Fangqing were both present. The two answered in the same words: "Losing at backgammon means having no sons.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Renjie and Wang Fangqing were both present. The two answered in the same words: "Losing at backgammon means having no sons.

sentences.zh: 天其意者以儆陛下乎！

translations.literal: Might Heaven's intent be to warn Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: Might Heaven's intent be to warn Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 且太子，天下本，本一搖，天下危矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, the crown prince is the root of the realm. Once the root is shaken, the realm is in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the crown prince is the root of the realm. Once the root is shaken, the realm is in peril.

sentences.zh: 文皇帝身蹈鋒鏑，勤勞而有天下，傳之子孫。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu himself braved blades and arrows, toiled in hardship, and won the realm, passing it to his sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu himself braved blades and arrows, toiled in hardship, and won the realm, passing it to his sons and grandsons.

sentences.zh: 先帝寢疾，詔陛下監國。

translations.literal: When the late emperor lay ill, he issued an edict that Your Majesty should oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor lay ill, he issued an edict that Your Majesty should oversee the state.

sentences.zh: 陛下掩神器而取之，十有餘年，又欲以三思爲後。

translations.literal: Your Majesty seized the imperial regalia and took the throne, and for more than ten years you have ruled—yet now you wish to make Sansi your successor.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty seized the imperial regalia and took the throne, and for more than ten years you have ruled—yet now you wish to make Sansi your successor.

sentences.zh: 且姑侄與母子孰親？

translations.literal: Moreover, which is closer—an aunt and nephew, or a mother and son?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, which is closer—an aunt and nephew, or a mother and son?

sentences.zh: 陛下立廬陵王，則千秋萬歳後常享宗廟；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty establishes the Prince of Luling, then after a thousand autumns and ten thousand years you will forever enjoy offerings in the ancestral temple;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty establishes the Prince of Luling, then after a thousand autumns and ten thousand years you will forever enjoy offerings in the ancestral temple;

sentences.zh: 三思立，廟不祔姑。」

translations.literal: if Sansi is established, the temple will not enshrine an aunt."
translations.idiomatic: if Sansi is established, the temple will not enshrine an aunt."

sentences.zh: 后感悟，即日遣徐彥伯迎廬陵王於房州。

translations.literal: The Empress was moved to understanding. That very day she dispatched Xu Yanbo to welcome the Prince of Luling from Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress was moved to understanding. That very day she dispatched Xu Yanbo to welcome the Prince of Luling from Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 王至，后匿王帳中，召見仁傑語廬陵事。

translations.literal: When the prince arrived, the Empress hid him in her tent and summoned Renjie to speak of the matter of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince arrived, the Empress hid him in her tent and summoned Renjie to speak of the matter of Luling.

sentences.zh: 仁傑敷請切至，涕下不能止。

translations.literal: Renjie pleaded earnestly and urgently, tears streaming down without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie pleaded earnestly and urgently, tears streaming down without cease.

sentences.zh: 后乃使王出，曰：「還爾太子！」

translations.literal: The Empress then had the prince come out and said: "I restore your crown princeship!
translations.idiomatic: The Empress then had the prince come out and said: "I restore your crown princeship!

sentences.zh: 仁傑降拜頓首，曰：「太子歸，未有知者，人言紛紛，何所信？」

translations.literal: Renjie bowed low and knocked his head on the ground, saying: "The crown prince has returned, but no one yet knows of it. With rumors flying everywhere, what can people believe?"
translations.idiomatic: Renjie bowed low and kowtowed on the ground, saying: "The crown prince has returned, but no one yet knows of it. With rumors flying everywhere, what can people believe?"

sentences.zh: 后然之。

translations.literal: The Empress agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress agreed.

sentences.zh: 更令太子舍龍門。

translations.literal: She further ordered the crown prince to lodge at Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: She further ordered the crown prince to lodge at Longmen.

sentences.zh: 具禮迎還，中外大悅。

translations.literal: With full ceremony he was welcomed back, and court and country rejoiced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: With full ceremony he was welcomed back, and court and country rejoiced greatly.

sentences.zh: 初，吉頊、李昭德數請還太子，而后意不回，唯仁傑毎以母子天性爲言，后雖忮忍，不能無感，故卒復唐嗣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ji Xu and Li Zhaode had repeatedly requested the restoration of the crown prince, but the Empress's mind did not turn back. Only Renjie spoke each time of the natural bond between mother and son. Though the Empress was jealous and cruel, she could not remain unmoved, and so in the end the succession of Tang was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ji Xu and Li Zhaode had repeatedly requested the restoration of the crown prince, but the Empress's mind did not turn back. Only Renjie spoke each time of the natural bond between mother and son. Though the Empress was jealous and cruel, she could not remain unmoved, and so in the end the succession of Tang was restored.

sentences.zh: 尋拜納言，兼右肅政御史大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Chief Minister of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Right Censor-in-Chief of the Suzheng Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Chief Minister of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Right Censor-in-Chief of the Suzheng Bureau.

sentences.zh: 突厥入趙、定，殺掠甚眾，詔仁傑爲河北道行軍元帥，假以便宜。

translations.literal: The Turks entered Zhao and Ding, killing and plundering in great numbers. An edict appointed Renjie Marshal of the Hebei Circuit campaign army and granted him discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks entered Zhao and Ding, killing and plundering in great numbers. An edict appointed Renjie Marshal of the Hebei Circuit campaign army and granted him discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 突厥盡殺所得男女萬計，由五回道去，仁傑追不能逮。

translations.literal: The Turks slaughtered all the men and women they had taken, numbering in the tens of thousands, and departed by the Wuhui route. Renjie pursued but could not overtake them.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks slaughtered all the men and women they had taken, numbering in the tens of thousands, and departed by the Wuhui route. Renjie pursued but could not overtake them.

sentences.zh: 更拜河北安撫大使。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Commissioner for Pacification of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed Commissioner for Pacification of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 時民多脅從於賊，賊已去，懼誅，逃匿。

translations.literal: At the time many common people had been compelled to follow the bandits. After the bandits had gone, they feared punishment and fled into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many common people had been compelled to follow the bandits. After the bandits had gone, they feared punishment and fled into hiding.

sentences.zh: 仁傑上疏曰：「議者以爲虜入寇，始明人之逆順，或迫脅，或願從，或受偽官，或爲招慰。

translations.literal: Renjie submitted a memorial, saying: "Those who discuss the matter hold that when the barbarians invaded, it first became clear who among the people were rebellious or loyal. Some were coerced, some willingly followed, some accepted false offices, and some served as recruiters and pacifiers.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie submitted a memorial, saying: "Those who discuss the matter hold that when the barbarians invaded, it first became clear who among the people were rebellious or loyal. Some were coerced, some willingly followed, some accepted false offices, and some served as recruiters and pacifiers.

sentences.zh: 誠以山東之人重氣，一往死不爲悔。

translations.literal: Truly the people of the eastern lands value honor; once they go forward they do not regret even unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Truly the people of the eastern lands value honor; once they go forward they do not regret even unto death.

sentences.zh: 比緣軍興，調發煩重，傷破家產，剔屋賣田，人不爲售。

translations.literal: Recently, because of military mobilization, levies and conscription have been burdensome and heavy, ruining households and breaking up estates. People stripped their houses and sold their fields, yet found no buyers.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, because of military mobilization, levies and conscription have been burdensome and heavy, ruining households and breaking up estates. People stripped their houses and sold their fields, yet found no buyers.

sentences.zh: 又官吏侵漁，州縣科役，督趣鞭笞，情危事迫，不循禮義，投跡犬羊，以圖賒死，此君子所愧，而小人之常。

translations.literal: Moreover, officials preyed upon them, and prefectures and counties imposed corvée and taxes, driving them on with whips and beatings. When feelings were desperate and circumstances pressing, they abandoned ritual and righteousness and cast their lot with barbarians to seek a reprieve from death. This is what gentlemen would be ashamed of, but what petty men commonly do.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, officials preyed upon them, and prefectures and counties imposed corvée and taxes, driving them on with whips and beatings. When feelings were desperate and circumstances pressing, they abandoned ritual and righteousness and cast their lot with barbarians to seek a reprieve from death. This is what gentlemen would be ashamed of, but what petty men commonly do.

sentences.zh: 民猶水也，壅則爲淵，疏則爲川，通塞隨流，豈有常性。

translations.literal: The people are like water: dammed up they become a deep pool; opened they become a river. Whether blocked or flowing follows the current—how could they have a fixed nature?
translations.idiomatic: The people are like water: dammed up they become a deep pool; opened they become a river. Whether blocked or flowing follows the current—how could they have a fixed nature?

sentences.zh: 昔董卓之亂，神器播越，卓已誅禽，部曲無赦，故事窮變生，流毒京室。

translations.literal: Formerly, in the turmoil of Dong Zhuo, the imperial regalia was cast adrift. After Zhuo was executed and captured, his followers were not pardoned. Because old cases reached their limit and new troubles arose, poison spread through the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, in the turmoil of Dong Zhuo, the imperial regalia was cast adrift. After Zhuo was executed and captured, his followers were not pardoned. Because old cases reached their limit and new troubles arose, poison spread through the capital.

sentences.zh: 此由恩不溥洽，失在機先。

translations.literal: This was because grace was not broadly applied, and the opportunity was lost beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: This was because grace was not broadly applied, and the opportunity was lost beforehand.

sentences.zh: 今負罪之伍，潛竄山澤，赦之則出，不赦則狂。

translations.literal: Now those burdened with guilt lurk hidden in mountains and marshes. If pardoned they will come out; if not pardoned they will run wild.
translations.idiomatic: Now those burdened with guilt lurk hidden in mountains and marshes. If pardoned they will come out; if not pardoned they will run wild.

sentences.zh: 山東群盜，緣茲聚結。

translations.literal: The bandits of the eastern lands are gathering on this account.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits of the eastern lands are gathering on this account.

sentences.zh: 故臣以爲邊鄙暫警不足憂，中土不寧可爲慮也。

translations.literal: Therefore your servant holds that a temporary alarm on the border is not worth worrying over, but unrest in the central lands is what should be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore your servant holds that a temporary alarm on the border is not worth worrying over, but unrest in the central lands is what should be feared.

sentences.zh: 夫持大國者不可以小治，事廣者不可以細分。

translations.literal: One who holds a great state cannot govern it with petty measures; one who handles broad affairs cannot divide them into minute parts.
translations.idiomatic: One who holds a great state cannot govern it with petty measures; one who handles broad affairs cannot divide them into minute parts.

sentences.zh: 人主所務，弗檢常法。

translations.literal: What a ruler should devote himself to is not inspecting every ordinary law.
translations.idiomatic: What a ruler should devote himself to is not inspecting every ordinary law.

sentences.zh: 願曲赦河北，一不問罪。」

translations.literal: I wish that a special pardon be granted to Hebei, with no one questioned for guilt.
translations.idiomatic: I wish that a special pardon be granted to Hebei, with no one questioned for guilt.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 還，除內史。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 后幸三陽宮，王公皆從，獨賜仁傑第一區，眷禮卓異，時無輩者。

translations.literal: When the Empress visited the Sanyang Palace, princes and ministers all followed, but Renjie alone was granted the finest residence. The favor shown him was extraordinary, and at the time none could compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress visited the Sanyang Palace, princes and ministers all followed, but Renjie alone was granted the finest residence. The favor shown him was extraordinary, and at the time none could compare with him.

sentences.zh: 是時李楷固、駱務整討契丹，克之，獻俘含樞殿，后大悅。

translations.literal: At that time Li Kaigu and Luo Wuzheng campaigned against the Khitans, defeated them, and presented captives in the Hanqu Hall. The Empress was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Kaigu and Luo Wuzheng campaigned against the Khitans, defeated them, and presented captives in the Hanqu Hall. The Empress was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 二人者，本契丹李盡忠部將，盡忠入寇，楷固等數挫王師，后降，有司請論如法。

translations.literal: These two men had originally been generals under the Khitan Li Jinzhong. When Jinzhong invaded, Kaigu and the others repeatedly defeated the imperial armies. After they submitted, the responsible officials requested that they be judged according to law.
translations.idiomatic: These two men had originally been generals under the Khitan Li Jinzhong. When Jinzhong invaded, Kaigu and the others repeatedly defeated the imperial armies. After they submitted, the responsible officials requested that they be judged according to law.

sentences.zh: 仁傑稱其驍勇可任，若貸死，必感恩納節，可以責功。

translations.literal: Renjie praised their valor as fit for employment. If their lives were spared, they would surely repay the grace and accept discipline, and could be charged with achieving merit.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie praised their valor as fit for employment. If their lives were spared, they would surely repay the grace and accept discipline, and could be charged with achieving merit.

sentences.zh: 至是凱旋，后舉酒屬仁傑，賞其知人。

translations.literal: When they now returned in triumph, the Empress raised a cup to Renjie and rewarded him for knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: When they now returned in triumph, the Empress raised a cup to Renjie and rewarded him for knowing men.

sentences.zh: 授楷固左玉鈐衞大將軍、燕國公，賜姓武；

translations.literal: Kaigu was appointed General of the Left Yulin Guard and Duke of Yan, and granted the surname Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Kaigu was appointed General of the Left Yulin Guard and Duke of Yan, and granted the surname Wu;

sentences.zh: 務整右武威衞將軍。

translations.literal: Wuzheng was appointed General of the Right Wuwei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzheng was appointed General of the Right Wuwei Guard.

sentences.zh: 后將造浮屠大像，度費數百萬，官不能足，更詔天下僧日施一錢助之。

translations.literal: The Empress was about to build a great Buddhist statue. The estimated cost was several million, and the treasury could not cover it. She further issued an edict that monks throughout the realm should contribute one coin per day to assist the project.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress was about to build a great Buddhist statue. The estimated cost was several million, and the treasury could not cover it. She further issued an edict that monks throughout the realm should contribute one coin per day to assist the project.

sentences.zh: 仁傑諫曰：「工不役鬼，必在役人；

translations.literal: Renjie admonished the throne, saying: "If labor does not employ ghosts, it must employ men;
translations.idiomatic: Renjie memorialized the throne, saying: "If labor does not employ ghosts, it must employ men;

sentences.zh: 物不天降，終由地出。

translations.literal: if materials do not fall from Heaven, they must ultimately come from the earth.
translations.idiomatic: if materials do not fall from Heaven, they must ultimately come from the earth.

sentences.zh: 不損百姓，且將何求？

translations.literal: If the common people are not harmed, from what source will you seek them?
translations.idiomatic: If the common people are not harmed, from what source will you seek them?

sentences.zh: 今邊垂未寧，宜寬征鎮之傜，省不急之務。

translations.literal: Now the frontiers are not yet settled. It is fitting to lighten the corvée of the border garrisons and reduce non-urgent undertakings.
translations.idiomatic: Now the frontiers are not yet settled. It is fitting to lighten the corvée of the border garrisons and reduce non-urgent undertakings.

sentences.zh: 就令顧作，以濟窮人，既失農時，是爲棄本。

translations.literal: Even if one were to look to forced labor to aid the poor, it would still miss the farming season and thus abandon the root.
translations.idiomatic: Even if one were to look to forced labor to aid the poor, it would still miss the farming season and thus abandon the root.

sentences.zh: 且無官助，理不得成。

translations.literal: Moreover, without official assistance, by reason it cannot be completed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, without official assistance, by reason it cannot be completed.

sentences.zh: 既費官財，又竭人力，一方有難，何以救之？」

translations.literal: It would both waste official funds and exhaust human labor. If trouble arose in one region, with what would you rescue it?
translations.idiomatic: It would both waste official funds and exhaust human labor. If trouble arose in one region, with what would you rescue it?

sentences.zh: 后由是罷役。

translations.literal: Because of this the Empress halted the project.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the Empress halted the project.

sentences.zh: 聖曆三年卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengli he died, at the age of seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Shengli era he died, at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 贈文昌右相，諡曰文惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of Right Minister of the Wenchang Hall, with the posthumous name Wen Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of Right Minister of the Wenchang Hall, with the posthumous name Wen Hui.

sentences.zh: 仁傑所薦進，若張柬之、桓彥範、敬暉、姚崇等，皆爲中興名臣。

translations.literal: Those whom Renjie recommended and advanced, such as Zhang Jianzhi, Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, and Yao Chong, all became famous ministers of the restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Those whom Renjie recommended and advanced, such as Zhang Jianzhi, Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, and Yao Chong, all became famous ministers of the restoration.

sentences.zh: 始居母喪，有白鵲馴擾之祥。

translations.literal: When he first observed mourning for his mother, there was an auspicious sign of white magpies coming tamely and hovering about.
translations.idiomatic: When he first observed mourning for his mother, there was an auspicious sign of white magpies coming tamely and hovering about.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，追贈司空。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong ascended the throne, Renjie was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong ascended the throne, Renjie was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 睿宗又封梁國公。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong further enfeoffed him as Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong further enfeoffed him as Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 子光嗣、景暉。

translations.literal: His sons were Guangsi and Jinghui.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Guangsi and Jinghui.

sentences.zh: 仁傑子 光嗣光嗣，聖曆初，爲司府丞。

translations.literal: Di Renjie's son Guangsi — Guangsi, at the beginning of the Shengli era, served as Assistant Director of the Court of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie's son Guangsi, in the early Shengli era, served as Assistant Director of the Court of the Treasury.

sentences.zh: 武后詔宰相各舉尚書郎一人，仁傑薦光嗣，由是拜地官員外郎，以稱職聞。

translations.literal: Empress Wu ordered that each chief minister recommend one Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; Renjie recommended Guangsi, and he was thereby appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, becoming known for competent service.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu ordered each chief minister to recommend one Gentleman of the Masters of Writing. Renjie recommended Guangsi, who was then appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and gained a reputation for competent service.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「祁奚內舉，果得人。」

translations.literal: The Empress said, "Qi Xi recommended from within his own family, and truly found the right man.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress said, "Like Qi Xi, who recommended a man from his own household, you have indeed found the right man.

sentences.zh: 歷淄、許、貝三州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively served as Prefect of Zi, Xu, and Bei prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as prefect of Zi, Xu, and Bei.

sentences.zh: 母喪，奪爲太府少卿，固讓，睿宗嘉其誠，許之。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he was recalled from mourning to serve as Vice Director of the Court of the Grand Treasury; he firmly declined, and Emperor Ruizong praised his sincerity and granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother, he was recalled to serve as Vice Director of the Court of the Grand Treasury, but he firmly declined. Emperor Ruizong praised his sincerity and allowed him to remain in mourning.

sentences.zh: 累遷揚州長史，以罪貶歙州別駕，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Senior Administrator of Yangzhou, then demoted to Vice Prefect of Shezhou on account of a crime, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Senior Administrator of Yangzhou, but was later demoted to Vice Prefect of Shezhou for an offense and died there.

sentences.zh: 景暉，官魏州司功參軍，貪暴爲虐，民苦之，因共毀其父生祠，不復奉。

translations.literal: Jinghui held the post of Recording Officer of Wei Prefecture; greedy and violent, he tyrannized the people. The people suffered under him and together destroyed his father's living shrine, never honoring it again.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghui served as Recording Officer of Wei Prefecture. Greedy and brutal, he tyrannized the people until they together tore down his father's living shrine and ceased to maintain it.

sentences.zh: 至元和中，田弘正鎮魏博，始奏葺之，血食不絶。

translations.literal: By the Yuanhe era, when Tian Hongzheng governed Weibo, he first memorialized to repair it, and sacrificial offerings did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era, when Tian Hongzheng governed Weibo, he memorialized the throne to have the shrine restored, and sacrifices were once again offered without interruption.

sentences.zh: 族孫兼謨。

translations.literal: A clansman-grandson, Jianmo.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman-grandson was Jianmo.

sentences.zh: 仁傑族孫 兼謨兼謨字汝諧，及進士第。

translations.literal: Di Renjie's clansman-grandson Jianmo — Jianmo, styled Ru'xie, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Di Renjie's clansman-grandson Jianmo, whose courtesy name was Ru'xie, passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 辟襄陽使府，剛正有祖風。

translations.literal: He was recruited to the commissioner's staff at Xiangyang; upright and firm, he bore the manner of his ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Recruited to the commissioner's staff at Xiangyang, he was upright and resolute, bearing something of his ancestor's character.

sentences.zh: 令狐楚執政，薦授左拾遺，數上書言事。

translations.literal: When Linghu Chu held power, he recommended Jianmo and had him appointed Left Reminder; he repeatedly submitted memorials on affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: When Linghu Chu came to power, he recommended Jianmo for appointment as Left Reminder, and Jianmo repeatedly submitted memorials on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 曆刑部郎中、蘄鄧鄭三州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively served as Director in the Ministry of Justice and as Prefect of Qi, Deng, and Zheng prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Director in the Ministry of Justice and as prefect of Qi, Deng, and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 歳旱饑，發粟賑濟，民人不流徙。

translations.literal: In a year of drought and famine, he distributed grain to relieve distress, and the people did not drift away in migration.
translations.idiomatic: During a year of drought and famine, he distributed grain for relief, and the people did not flee the region.

sentences.zh: 改蘇州，以治最，擢給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Suzhou; for the excellence of his governance he was promoted to Supervisor of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Suzhou, he was promoted to Supervisor of Attendants for the excellence of his governance.

sentences.zh: 左藏史盜度支縑帛，文宗以經赦詔勿治，兼謨封還詔書，帝問之，對曰：「典史犯贓，不可免。」

translations.literal: A clerk of the Left Storehouse stole silk from the Department of Revenue; Emperor Wenzong, citing a general amnesty, ordered that the case not be prosecuted. Jianmo sealed and returned the edict. When the Emperor questioned him, he replied, "The clerk committed corruption; he cannot be exempted.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk of the Left Storehouse stole silk from the Department of Revenue. Emperor Wenzong, citing a general amnesty, ordered that the case not be prosecuted, but Jianmo sealed and returned the edict. When the Emperor questioned him, he replied, "A clerk who commits corruption cannot go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕已赦其長官，吏亦宜宥，與其失信，甯失罪人。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "I have already pardoned his superior; the clerk should also be forgiven — better to break one's word than to let the guilty go free.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I have already pardoned his superior; the clerk should be forgiven as well — better to break one's word than to let a guilty man go free.

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「後或事有不可，勿以還詔爲憚。」

translations.literal: Then he added, "If hereafter something should prove unacceptable, do not shrink from returning an edict.
translations.idiomatic: Then he added, "If hereafter something proves unacceptable, do not hesitate to return an edict.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「御史臺朝廷綱紀，一臺正，則朝廷治，朝廷正，則天下治。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "The Censorate is the regulatory standard of the court — when one bureau is upright, the court is well governed; when the court is upright, the realm is well governed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The Censorate holds the regulatory standard of the court. When that bureau is upright, the court is well governed; when the court is upright, the realm is well governed.

sentences.zh: 畏忌顧望，則職業廢矣。

translations.literal: If one fears and hesitates, looking this way and that, then one's duties are abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: If you fear consequences and hang back, your duties are lost.

sentences.zh: 卿，梁公後，當嗣家聲，不可不慎。」

translations.literal: You are a descendant of the Duke of Liang; you should carry on the family's renown — you must not be careless.
translations.idiomatic: You are a descendant of Duke of Liang Di Renjie; you should carry on your family's renown — you must not be careless.

sentences.zh: 兼謨頓首謝。

translations.literal: Jianmo prostrated himself and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Jianmo prostrated himself in thanks.

sentences.zh: 江西觀察使呉士矩加給其軍，擅用上供錢數十萬。

translations.literal: Wu Shiju, Observation Commissioner of Jiangxi, made additional allotments to his army and on his own authority used several hundred thousand strings of tribute money.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shiju, Observation Commissioner of Jiangxi, made extra payments to his troops and on his own authority spent several hundred thousand strings of tribute funds.

sentences.zh: 兼謨劾奏：「觀察使爲陛下守土，宣國詔條，知臨戎賞士，州有定數，而與奪由己，貽弊一方，爲諸道觖望，請付有司治罪。」

translations.literal: Jianmo impeached him, memorializing: "An observation commissioner guards territory for Your Majesty and should proclaim the statutes of the state. He knows that rewards for troops on campaign have fixed quotas by prefecture, yet he granted and withheld at his own discretion, bequeathing harm to one region and arousing resentment in other circuits. I ask that he be handed over to the relevant offices for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Jianmo impeached him, writing: "An observation commissioner guards territory on Your Majesty's behalf and should proclaim the laws of the land. He knows that rewards for troops on campaign have fixed quotas set by prefecture, yet he granted and withheld at his own whim, bequeathing harm on one region and stirring resentment throughout the other circuits. I ask that he be handed over to the proper authorities for punishment.

sentences.zh: 士矩繇是貶蔡州別駕。

translations.literal: Shiju was thereby demoted to Vice Prefect of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shiju was thereby demoted to Vice Prefect of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 曆兵部侍郎、河東節度使。

translations.literal: He successively served as Vice Minister of War and Military Commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Vice Minister of War and Military Commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 還爲尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 武宗子峴封益王，命兼謨爲傅。

translations.literal: Prince Xian, son of Emperor Wuzong, was enfeoffed as Prince of Yi, and Jianmo was appointed his Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong's son Prince Xian was enfeoffed as Prince of Yi, Jianmo was appointed his tutor.

sentences.zh: 俄領天平節度使，辭疾，以秘書監歸洛陽，遷東都留守，卒。

translations.literal: Soon he also served as Military Commissioner of Tianping; citing illness, he retired to Luoyang as Director of the Secretariat, was transferred to Defender of the Eastern Capital, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also served as Military Commissioner of Tianping. Citing illness, he retired to Luoyang as Director of the Secretariat, was later appointed Defender of the Eastern Capital, and died there.

sentences.zh: 郝處俊郝處俊，安州安陸人。

translations.literal: Hao Chujun — Hao Chujun was a native of Anlu in Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Chujun was a native of Anlu in Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 父相貴，因隋亂，與婦翁許紹據峽州，歸國，拜滁州刺史，封甑山縣公。

translations.literal: His father Xianggui, amid the disorder of the Sui, together with his father-in-law Xu Shao seized control of Xiazhou; after submitting to the new dynasty he was appointed Prefect of Chuzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Zengshan County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xianggui, during the chaos of the Sui collapse, joined his father-in-law Xu Shao in holding Xiazhou. After submitting to the Tang, he was appointed Prefect of Chuzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Zengshan County.

sentences.zh: 處俊甫十歳而孤，故吏歸千縑賵之，已能讓不受。

translations.literal: Chujun was orphaned at the age of ten; a former subordinate of his father brought a thousand rolls of silk as mourning gifts, yet even then he knew to defer and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Chujun was orphaned at ten. A former subordinate of his father brought a thousand rolls of silk as mourning gifts, but even then he knew to decline and would not accept them.

sentences.zh: 及長，好學，嗜《漢書》，崖略暗誦。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he loved learning and was devoted to the Book of Han, able to recite it from memory in broad outline.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up, he loved learning and was devoted to the Book of Han, able to recite it from memory in broad outline.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，第進士，解褐著作佐郎，襲父爵。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he passed the jinshi examination, entered service as Assistant Editor in the Palace Library, and inherited his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he passed the jinshi examination, entered service as Assistant Editor in the Palace Library, and inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 兄弟友睦，事諸舅謹甚。

translations.literal: He and his brothers were friendly and harmonious, and he served his maternal uncles with great care.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in friendly harmony with his brothers and served his maternal uncles with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 再轉滕王友，恥爲王府屬，棄官去。

translations.literal: After two appointments as Companion to the Prince of Teng, he felt ashamed to be a retainer of the princely household and abandoned his office and left.
translations.idiomatic: After serving twice as Companion to the Prince of Teng, he felt ashamed to be a retainer of a princely household and resigned his office.

sentences.zh: 久之，召拜太子司議郎，累遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: After some time he was summoned and appointed Master of Ceremonies to the Heir Apparent, and was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was summoned to serve as Master of Ceremonies to the Heir Apparent and rose in succession to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 高麗叛，詔李勣爲浿江道大總管，處俊副之。

translations.literal: When Goguryeo rebelled, Li Ji was ordered to serve as Grand Commander of the Bijiang Circuit, with Chujun as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Goguryeo rebelled, Li Ji was ordered to serve as Grand Commander of the Bijiang Circuit, with Chujun as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 師入虜境，未陣，賊遽至，舉軍危駭。

translations.literal: When the army entered enemy territory and had not yet formed ranks, the rebels suddenly arrived, and the whole army was stricken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: The army had entered enemy territory but had not yet formed ranks when the rebels suddenly appeared, filling the entire force with dread.

sentences.zh: 處俊方據胡床，體胖，安餐乾Я不顧，密畀料精銳擊之，虜卻，眾壯其謀。

translations.literal: Chujun was just then seated on a camp stool; corpulent, he calmly ate dry rations without paying heed, secretly sent elite troops to strike them, and the barbarians withdrew. The troops admired his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Chujun was seated on a camp stool, corpulent and calm, eating dry rations without a glance at the enemy while secretly dispatching picked troops to strike. The barbarians withdrew, and the troops admired his strategy.

sentences.zh: 入拜東臺侍郎。
