translations.literal: He entered court and was appointed Vice Director of the Eastern Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court and was appointed Vice Director of the Eastern Terrace.

sentences.zh: 時浮屠盧伽逸多治丹，曰：「可以續年。」

translations.literal: At the time the monk Luoqieduo was compounding elixirs, saying, "They can prolong life.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the monk Luoqieduo was compounding elixirs, claiming they could prolong life.

sentences.zh: 高宗欲遂餌之，處俊諫曰：「脩短固有命，異方之劑，安得輕服哉？

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong wished to take them forthwith. Chujun remonstrated, saying, "Long or short life is fixed by fate — how can one lightly swallow drugs from foreign lands?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong wished to take them at once, but Chujun remonstrated: "Long or short life is fixed by fate — how can one lightly swallow remedies from foreign lands?

sentences.zh: 昔先帝詔浮屠那羅邇娑寐案其方書爲秘劑，取靈怪石，曆歳乃能就。

translations.literal: Formerly the late Emperor ordered the monk Narayanasleep to examine his formulary and prepare a secret elixir, gathering spirit stones; only after several years could it be completed.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the late Emperor ordered the monk Narayanasleep to examine his formulary and prepare a secret elixir from spirit stones, and only after several years was it finished.

sentences.zh: 先帝餌之，俄而大漸，上醫不知所爲。

translations.literal: The late Emperor took it, and soon grew gravely ill; the court physicians did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor took the elixir, and soon grew gravely ill, while the court physicians knew not what to do.

sentences.zh: 群臣請顯戮其人，議者以爲取笑夷狄，故法不得行。

translations.literal: The ministers asked that the man be publicly executed, but debaters held that this would make a laughingstock before the barbarians, so the law could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers asked that the man be publicly executed, but others argued that this would invite mockery from the barbarian peoples, and so the law could not be applied.

sentences.zh: 前鑒不遠，惟陛下深察。」

translations.literal: The recent lesson is not far off — I ask only that Your Majesty examine the matter deeply.
translations.idiomatic: That recent lesson is not far behind us — I ask only that Your Majesty examine this deeply.

sentences.zh: 帝納其言，第拜盧伽逸多爲懷化大將軍，進處俊同東西臺三品。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted his words, merely granting Luoqieduo the title of General of Cherishing Transformation, and promoting Chujun to Third Rank concurrently of the Eastern and Western Terraces.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted his counsel, merely granting Luoqieduo the title of General of Cherishing Transformation while promoting Chujun to Third Rank concurrently of the Eastern and Western Terraces.

sentences.zh: 咸亨初，幸東都，皇太子監國，諸宰相皆留，而處俊獨從。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianheng era, when the Emperor visited the Eastern Capital, the Crown Prince supervised the realm; all the chief ministers remained behind, but Chujun alone accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xianheng era, when the Emperor visited the Eastern Capital and the Crown Prince supervised the realm, all the chief ministers remained at court — only Chujun accompanied the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗曰：「王者無外，何爲守禦？

translations.literal: The Emperor once said, "A sovereign has no 'outside' — why maintain defenses?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once said, "A sovereign has no 'outside' — why then maintain defenses?

sentences.zh: 而重門擊柝，庸待不虞邪？

translations.literal: Yet heavy gates and watchmen beating clappers — is this how one awaits the unexpected?
translations.idiomatic: Heavy gates and watchmen beating the night clapper — is that how one waits for the unexpected?

sentences.zh: 我嘗疑秦法爲寬，荊軻匹夫耳，匕首竊發，群臣皆荷戟侍，莫敢拒，豈非習慢使然？」

translations.literal: I once doubted whether Qin law was too lenient — Jing Ke was but a common man; he secretly drew a dagger, and though all the ministers stood bearing halberds on guard, none dared resist. Was this not caused by habit bred of laxity?
translations.idiomatic: I once suspected that Qin law was too lenient. Jing Ke was but a common man, yet when he secretly drew a dagger, all the ministers stood by bearing halberds and none dared resist — was this not the result of habits bred from laxity?

sentences.zh: 處俊對曰：「此乃法急耳。

translations.literal: Chujun replied, "This is rather a matter of law being too severe.
translations.idiomatic: Chujun replied, "This is rather a matter of law being too severe.

sentences.zh: 秦法，輒升殿者，夷三族。

translations.literal: Under Qin law, anyone who rashly ascended the hall would have three generations exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin law, anyone who rashly mounted the hall would have three generations exterminated.

sentences.zh: 人皆懼族，安有敢拒邪？

translations.literal: When all men feared extermination of their clans, how could any dare resist?
translations.idiomatic: When everyone feared the extinction of their clan, who would dare resist?

sentences.zh: 魏曹操著令曰；

translations.literal: Cao Cao of Wei issued an order, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao of Wei issued an order, saying:

sentences.zh: 『京城有變，九卿各守其府。』

translations.literal: 'If turmoil arises in the capital, each of the Nine Ministers shall keep to his office.
translations.idiomatic: 'If turmoil arises in the capital, each of the Nine Ministers shall keep to his office.

sentences.zh: 後嚴才亂，與徒數十人攻左掖門，操登銅爵臺望之，無敢救者。

translations.literal: Later Yan Cai rebelled with several dozen followers and attacked the Left Flanking Gate. Cao mounted the Bronze Bird Terrace to watch — none dared go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yan Cai rebelled with several dozen followers and attacked the Left Flanking Gate. Cao mounted the Bronze Bird Terrace to watch, and none dared go to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 時王脩爲奉常，聞變，召車騎未至，領官屬歩至宮門。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Xiu served as Director of Ceremonies; hearing of the disturbance, he summoned his carriage, but before it arrived he led his subordinates on foot to the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Xiu was Director of Ceremonies. Hearing of the disturbance, he summoned his carriage, but before it arrived he led his subordinates on foot to the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 操曰；

translations.literal: Cao said:
translations.idiomatic: Cao said:

sentences.zh: '彼來者，必王脩乎！

translations.literal: He who comes must be Wang Xiu!
translations.idiomatic: The man who comes must be Wang Xiu!

sentences.zh: '此由脩察變識幾，故冒法赴難。

translations.literal: This was because Xiu discerned the change and recognized the critical moment, and so defied the law to go to the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: This was because Xiu had discerned the disturbance and recognized the critical moment, and so defied the law to go to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 向若拘常，則遂成禍矣。

translations.literal: Had he kept to convention, disaster would have followed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Had he kept to convention, disaster would have ensued at once.

sentences.zh: 故王者設法不可急，亦不可慢。

translations.literal: Thus when a sovereign establishes law, it must be neither too severe nor too lax.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when a sovereign establishes law, it must be neither too severe nor too lax.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰'不懈於位，人之攸塈'，仁也；

translations.literal: The Book of Poetry says, 'Never slack in office — this gives men peace,' which is benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Poetry says, 'Never slack in office — this gives men peace' — this is benevolence;

sentences.zh: '式遏寇虐，無俾作慝'，刑也。

translations.literal: Repress the violent and cruel — do not allow wickedness' — this is punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Repress the violent and cruel — do not allow wickedness' — this is punishment.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰'高明柔克，沈潛剛克'，中道也。」

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says, 'What is lofty and bright is overcome by gentleness; what is deep and hidden is overcome by firmness' — this is the middle way.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, 'What is lofty and bright is overcome by gentleness; what is deep and hidden is overcome by firmness' — this is the middle way.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Well spoken."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Well spoken."

sentences.zh: 轉中書侍郎，監脩國史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and oversaw the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and placed in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 初，顯慶中，令狐德棻、劉胤之撰國史，其後許敬宗復加緒次。

translations.literal: Initially, in the Xianqing era, Linghu Defen and Liu Yinzi compiled the national history; afterward Xu Jingzong added further arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Xianqing era, Linghu Defen and Liu Yinzi had compiled the national history; afterward Xu Jingzong revised and continued their work.

sentences.zh: 帝恨敬宗所紀失實，更命宰相刊正，且曰：「朕昔從幸未央宮，辟仗既過，有橫刀伏草中者，先帝斂轡卻，謂朕曰；

translations.literal: The Emperor resented that Jingzong's account was untrue and ordered the chief ministers to revise it, saying, "When I once followed on an excursion to Weiyang Palace, after the guard of honor had passed, a man with a broadsword lay hidden in the grass. The late Emperor reined in and drew back, and said to me:
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor resented that Jingzong's account was untrue and ordered the chief ministers to revise it, saying, "When I once accompanied the late Emperor on an excursion to Weiyang Palace, after the guard of honor had passed, a man with a broadsword lay hidden in the grass. The late Emperor reined in and drew back, saying to me:

sentences.zh: '事發，當死者數十人，汝可命出之。

translations.literal: If this incident comes to light, several dozen men will deserve death — you may order them released.
translations.idiomatic: If this comes to light, several dozen men will deserve death — you may order them released.

sentences.zh: '史臣惟敘此爲實。」

translations.literal: The historians should record only this as the truth.
translations.idiomatic: The historians should record only this as truth.

sentences.zh: 處俊曰：「先帝仁恩溥博，類非一。

translations.literal: Chujun said, "The late Emperor's benevolence and grace were broad and abundant — such examples were not one alone.
translations.idiomatic: Chujun said, "The late Emperor's benevolence and grace were broad and abundant — such examples were hardly unique.

sentences.zh: 臣之弟處傑被擇供奉，時有三衞誤拂禦衣者，懼甚。

translations.literal: My younger brother Chujie was selected for palace attendance; once three guards of the Three Guards accidentally brushed the Imperial robe, and were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: My younger brother Chujie was selected for palace attendance. Once three guards of the Three Guards accidentally brushed the Imperial robe and were terrified.

sentences.zh: 先帝曰：'左右無御史，我不汝罪。

translations.literal: The late Emperor said, 'With no censor at hand, I will not punish you.
translations.idiomatic: The late Emperor said, 'With no censor at hand, I will not punish you.

sentences.zh: '」帝曰：「此史臣應載。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "This the historians should record.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The historians should record this as well.

sentences.zh: 處俊乃表左史李仁實欲刪整偽辭，會仁實死而止。

translations.literal: Chujun thereupon memorialized that the Left Historian Li Renshi wished to revise and purge false language, but the matter ceased when Renshi died.
translations.idiomatic: Chujun thereupon memorialized that Left Historian Li Renshi wished to revise and purge false passages, but the effort stopped when Renshi died.

sentences.zh: 上元初，帝觀酺翔鸞閣，時赤縣與太常音技分東西朋，帝詔雍王賢主東，周王顯主西，因以角勝，處俊曰：「禮所以示童子無誑者，恐其欺詐之心生也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shangyuan era, the Emperor watched a feast at the Xiangluan Pavilion. The county officials and the musicians of the Court of Ceremonies divided into eastern and western factions; the Emperor ordered Prince Xian of Yong to head the east and Prince Xian of Zhou to head the west, and had them compete for victory. Chujun said, "Rites are meant to show children that there is no deception, lest the heart inclined to fraud be born.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shangyuan era, the Emperor watched a feast at the Xiangluan Pavilion. The county officials and the Court of Ceremonies musicians divided into eastern and western factions, and the Emperor ordered Prince Xian of Yong to lead the east and Prince Xian of Zhou the west, setting them to compete. Chujun said, "Rites are meant to show children that there must be no deceit, lest a heart inclined to fraud take root.

sentences.zh: 二王春秋少，意操未定，乃公朋造黨使相誇，彼俳兒優子，言辭無度，爭負勝，相譏誚，非所以導仁義，示雍和也。」

translations.literal: The two princes are young in years and their disposition is not yet settled — yet you openly form factions and parties and set them to vaunt one another. Those jesters and players speak without restraint, vying over victory and defeat and mocking one another — this is no way to guide them in benevolence and righteousness, nor to show harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The two princes are still young and their character is not yet settled, yet you openly form factions and set them to vaunt one another. Jesters and players speak without restraint, vying over victory and defeat and mocking one another — this is no way to guide them in benevolence and righteousness, nor to display harmony.

sentences.zh: 帝遽止，歎曰：「處俊遠識，非眾臣所逮。」

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately stopped it and sighed, "Chujun's far-sighted wisdom is what the multitude of ministers cannot match.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor immediately stopped the contest and sighed, "Chujun's far-sighted wisdom is beyond what the other ministers can reach.

sentences.zh: 遷中書令，兼太子賓客，檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Tutor to the Crown Prince and Acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat, concurrently serving as Tutor to the Crown Prince and Acting Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 帝多疾，欲遜位武后，處俊諫曰：「天子治陽道，後治陰德，然則帝與后猶日之與月，陽之與陰，各有所主，不相奪也。

translations.literal: The Emperor suffered frequent illness and wished to abdicate in favor of Empress Wu. Chujun remonstrated, saying, "The Son of Heaven governs the yang way, the empress the yin virtue — thus emperor and empress are like sun and moon, yang and yin, each with its own domain, neither usurping the other.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor suffered frequent illness and wished to abdicate in favor of Empress Wu. Chujun remonstrated, saying, "The Son of Heaven governs the yang way and the empress the yin virtue — emperor and empress are like sun and moon, yang and yin, each with its own domain, neither usurping the other.

sentences.zh: 若失其序，上謫見於天，下降災諸人。

translations.literal: If this order is lost, reproaches appear in Heaven above, and disasters descend upon the people below.
translations.idiomatic: If this order is lost, reproaches appear in heaven above and disasters descend upon the people below.

sentences.zh: 昔魏文帝著令，帝崩，不許皇后臨朝。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Wei issued an order that when the emperor dies, the empress is not permitted to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Wen of Wei decreed that when an emperor dies, the empress may not attend court.

sentences.zh: 今陛下奈何欲身傳位天后乎？

translations.literal: How then can Your Majesty now wish to transfer the throne in person to the Heavenly Empress?
translations.idiomatic: How then can Your Majesty wish to transfer the throne in your own lifetime to the Heavenly Empress?

sentences.zh: 天下者，高祖、太宗之天下，非陛下之天下，正應謹守宗廟，傳之子孫，不宜持國與人，以喪厥家。」

translations.literal: The realm belongs to Gaozu and Taizong — it is not Your Majesty's private possession. You should faithfully guard the ancestral temple and pass it to your sons and grandsons; you should not hand the state to another and thereby destroy your own house.
translations.idiomatic: The realm belongs to Gaozu and Taizong — it is not Your Majesty's to dispose of at will. You should faithfully guard the ancestral temple and pass the throne to your sons and grandsons, not hand the state to another and thereby destroy your own house.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎李義琰曰：「處俊言可從，惟陛下不疑。」

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Yiyan said, "Chujun's words should be followed — I ask only that Your Majesty have no doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Yiyan said, "Chujun's words should be heeded — I ask only that Your Majesty harbor no doubts.

sentences.zh: 事遂沮。

translations.literal: The matter was thereby thwarted.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was thereby abandoned.

sentences.zh: 又兼太子左庶子，拜侍中，罷爲太子少保。

translations.literal: He was also appointed concurrently Left Subordinate to the Crown Prince, promoted to Palace Attendant, then dismissed to serve as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed concurrently Left Subordinate to the Crown Prince and promoted to Palace Attendant, then dismissed to serve as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 開耀元年卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of the Kaiyao era, at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Kaiyao era, at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司、荊州大都督。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master of the Palace with Gold Seal and Ceremonial Regalia Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Grand Protector General of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master of the Palace with Gold Seal and Ceremonial Regalia Equal to the Three Excellencies and Grand Protector General of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝哀歎其忠，舉哀光順門，祭以少牢，賻絹布八百段、米粟八百石，詔百官赴哭，官庀葬事。

translations.literal: The Emperor mourned and lamented his loyalty, held mourning rites at the Guangshun Gate, and offered the secondary sacrifice. He granted eight hundred lengths of silk and cloth and eight hundred shi of grain as funeral gifts, ordered all officials to attend the mourning, and had the government arrange the burial.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor mourned his loyalty, held mourning rites at the Guangshun Gate, and offered the secondary sacrifice. He granted eight hundred lengths of silk and cloth and eight hundred shi of grain as funeral gifts, ordered all officials to attend the mourning, and had the government arrange the burial.

sentences.zh: 子北叟固辭，未聽。

translations.literal: His son Beisou firmly declined, but the Emperor would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Beisou firmly declined the honors, but the Emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 裴炎爲白帝曰：「處俊阽死，諉臣曰；

translations.literal: Pei Yan reported to the Emperor on his behalf, saying, "As Chujun lay near death, he charged me, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yan reported to the Emperor on his behalf, saying, "Near death, Chujun charged me, saying:

sentences.zh: '生無益于國，死無煩費，凡詔賜，願一罷之。

translations.literal: In life I brought no benefit to the state; in death I wish for no lavish expense — of all edicts and gifts, I ask that they be entirely cancelled.
translations.idiomatic: In life I brought no benefit to the state; in death I wish for no lavish expense — of all edicts and gifts, I ask that they be entirely cancelled.

sentences.zh: '」帝聞惻然，答其意，止賻物而已。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard this he was deeply moved, and in deference to his intent stopped at cancelling only the funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor heard this he was deeply moved, and in deference to Chujun's wish cancelled only the funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 處俊資約素，土木形骸，然臨事敢言，自秉政，在帝前議論諄諄，必傅經義，凡所規獻，得大臣體。

translations.literal: Chujun's substance was plain and simple — he was like clay and timber in bodily form — yet when affairs arose he dared to speak out. From the time he wielded power, before the Emperor his counsel was earnest and repeated, always grounded in the classics; in all that he proposed and presented, he bore the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Chujun was plain and unadorned in manner — a man of clay and timber in bodily form — yet when matters arose he dared to speak plainly. From the time he wielded power, his counsel before the Emperor was earnest and sustained, always grounded in the classics; in all he proposed and presented, he bore the dignity of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 武后雖忌之，以其操履無玷，不能害。

translations.literal: Although Empress Wu was jealous of him, because his conduct and bearing were without blemish, she could not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Although Empress Wu resented him, his conduct was without blemish and she could find no way to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 與舅許圉師同裏，俱宦達；

translations.literal: He and his maternal uncle Xu Yushi were from the same village; both achieved high office;
translations.idiomatic: He and his maternal uncle Xu Yushi came from the same village, and both rose to high office;

sentences.zh: 鄕人田氏、彭氏以高貲顯。

translations.literal: while fellow townsfolk of the Tian and Peng clans rose to prominence through great wealth.
translations.idiomatic: while fellow townsfolk of the Tian and Peng clans won renown through great wealth.

sentences.zh: 故江、淮間爲語曰：「貴如郝、許，富如田、彭。」

translations.literal: Hence among the Jiang and Huai regions a saying went: "As noble as the Haos and Xus, as rich as the Tians and Pengs.
translations.idiomatic: Hence a saying ran through the Jiang and Huai regions: "As noble as the Haos and Xus, as rich as the Tians and Pengs.

sentences.zh: 處俊孫 象賢孫象賢，垂拱中，爲太子通事舍人，后素銜處俊，故因事誅之。

translations.literal: Chujun's grandson Xiangxian — during the Zhonggong era he served as Master of Communications Attendant to the Crown Prince. The Empress had long borne a grudge against Chujun, so she used an incident as pretext to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Chujun's grandson Xiangxian served during the Zhonggong era as Master of Communications Attendant to the Crown Prince. The Empress had long nursed a grudge against Chujun, and so found a pretext to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，極罵乃死，后怒，令離磔其屍，斫夷祖、父棺塚。

translations.literal: At execution he cursed her to the utmost and then died. The Empress in fury ordered his corpse dismembered and scattered, and had his grandfather's and father's coffins smashed and tombs levelled.
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution, he cursed her without restraint until he died. The Empress in fury ordered his corpse torn apart and scattered, and had his grandfather's and father's coffins smashed and their tombs razed.

sentences.zh: 自是訖後世，將刑人，必先以木丸窒云。

translations.literal: From then until later ages, when about to execute someone, they would first stop up the mouth with a wooden gag — so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: From that time down through later ages, it is said, those about to be executed would first have their mouths stopped with wooden gags.

sentences.zh: 朱敬則朱敬則，字少連，亳州永城人。

translations.literal: Zhu Jingze, styled Shaolian, was a man of Yongcheng in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jingze, whose courtesy name was Shaolian, came from Yongcheng in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 以孝義世被旌顯，一門六闕相望。

translations.literal: His family's filial piety and righteousness had won imperial commendation generation after generation; six memorial gateways stood one after another in a single household.
translations.idiomatic: His family's filial piety and righteousness had won imperial commendation for generations; six memorial gateways stood in succession within a single household.

sentences.zh: 敬則志尚恢博，好學，重節義然諾，善與人交，振其急難，不責報於人。

translations.literal: Jingze's aspirations were broad and magnanimous. He loved learning, prized integrity and keeping his word, was skilled at friendship, and would rescue others in their emergencies without demanding repayment from them.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze's aspirations were broad and generous. He loved learning, prized integrity and keeping his word, was skilled at friendship, and would rescue others in distress without asking anything in return.

sentences.zh: 與左史江融、左僕射魏元忠善。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Left Historian Jiang Rong and Left Vice Director Wei Yuanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Left Historian Jiang Rong and Left Vice Director Wei Yuanzhong.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，高宗聞其名，召見，異之，爲中書令李敬玄所毀，故授洹水尉。

translations.literal: In the Xianheng era, Gaozong heard his name, summoned and met him, and was impressed — but Chief Minister Li Jingxuan slandered him, so he was appointed magistrate of Huanshui.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianheng era, Gaozong heard his name, summoned him for an audience, and was impressed — but Chief Minister Li Jingxuan slandered him, and so he was posted as magistrate of Huanshui.

sentences.zh: 久之，除右補闕。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed Right Remonstrance Officer.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Right Remonstrance Officer.

sentences.zh: 初，武后稱制，天下頗流言，遂開告密羅織之路，興大獄，誅將相大臣。

translations.literal: Initially, when Empress Wu held the reins of government, there was much seditious talk throughout the realm. She therefore opened the path of denunciation and fabricated charges, raised great trials, and executed generals, ministers, and great officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu first held the reins of government, seditious talk spread widely through the realm. She opened the path of secret denunciation and fabricated charges, raised great trials, and executed generals, ministers, and great officials.

sentences.zh: 至是，已革命，事益寧。

translations.literal: By now she had changed the dynasty; affairs grew ever more settled.
translations.idiomatic: By now she had changed the dynasty, and affairs were growing steadily more settled.

sentences.zh: 敬則諫曰：

translations.literal: Jingze remonstrated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jingze remonstrated, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞李斯之相秦也，行申、商之法，重刑名之家，杜私門；

translations.literal: I have heard that when Li Si served as chancellor of Qin, he implemented the laws of Shen Buhai and Shang Yang, emphasized the school of punitive names, and closed off private factions;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when Li Si served as chancellor of Qin, he implemented the laws of Shen Buhai and Shang Yang, emphasized the school of punitive names, and closed off private factions;

sentences.zh: 張公室；

translations.literal: enlarged the public household;
translations.idiomatic: and enlarged the public household;

sentences.zh: 棄無用之費，損不急之官；

translations.literal: discarded useless expenditures and reduced non-urgent offices;
translations.idiomatic: discarded useless expenditures and reduced non-urgent offices;

sentences.zh: 惜日愛功，亟戰疾耕。

translations.literal: cherished each day and loved achievement, fighting constantly and plowing urgently.
translations.idiomatic: cherished each day and loved achievement, fighting constantly and plowing urgently.

sentences.zh: 既庶而富，遂屠諸侯。

translations.literal: Once the populace was numerous and wealth abundant, he then destroyed the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Once the populace was numerous and the state was rich, he then destroyed the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 此救弊之術也。

translations.literal: This was the method of remedying decay.
translations.idiomatic: This was the method of remedying a failing age.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「刻薄可施子進趨，變詐可陳於攻戰。」

translations.literal: Hence it is said: "Harshness may be applied to those pressing forward in pursuit; deceit may be displayed in attack and battle.
translations.idiomatic: Hence it is said: "Harshness may be applied to those pressing forward in pursuit; deceit may be displayed in attack and battle.

sentences.zh: 天下已平，故可易之以寬簡，潤之以淳和。

translations.literal: When the realm was already pacified, one could therefore replace these with leniency and simplicity, and moisten it with pure harmony.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm was already pacified, one could replace these with leniency and simplicity, and nourish it with pure harmony.

sentences.zh: 秦乃不然，淫虐滋甚，往而不反，卒至土崩。

translations.literal: Yet Qin did not do so — debauchery and cruelty grew ever worse, pressing forward without turning back, until at last the realm collapsed like crumbling earth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qin did not do so — debauchery and cruelty grew ever worse, pressing forward without turning back, until at last the realm collapsed like crumbling earth.

sentences.zh: 此不知變之禍也。

translations.literal: This is the disaster of not knowing when to change.
translations.idiomatic: This is the disaster of not knowing when to change.

sentences.zh: 陸賈、叔孫通事漢祖，當滎陽、成皋間，糧餉窮，智勇困，未嘗敢開一説，效一奇，唯進豪猾貪暴之人。

translations.literal: Lu Jia and Shusun Tong served the Han founder. During the struggle between Xingyang and Chenggao, when provisions ran out and wit and courage were exhausted, they never dared offer a single proposal or present a single stratagem — they only recommended men who were overbearing, cunning, greedy, and violent.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jia and Shusun Tong served the Han founder. During the struggle between Xingyang and Chenggao, when provisions ran out and wit and courage were exhausted, they never dared offer a single proposal or present a single stratagem — they only recommended men who were overbearing, cunning, greedy, and violent.

sentences.zh: 及區宇適定，乃陳《詩》、《書》，説禮、樂，開王道。

translations.literal: Once the realm was just settling, they then set forth the Poetry and Documents, expounded ritual and music, and opened the way of the True King.
translations.idiomatic: Once the realm was just settling, they set forth the Poetry and Documents, expounded ritual and music, and opened the way of the True King.

sentences.zh: 高帝忿然曰：「吾以馬上得之，安事《詩》、《書》？」

translations.literal: The High Emperor said angrily, "I won the realm from horseback — what need have I for the Poetry and Documents?
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor said angrily, "I won the realm from horseback — what need have I for the Poetry and Documents?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「馬上得之，可馬上治之乎？」

translations.literal: They replied, "You won it from horseback — but can you govern it from horseback?
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "You won it from horseback — but can you govern it from horseback?

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The Emperor fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 於是賈著《新語》，通定禮儀。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jia wrote New Discourses, and Tong fixed the rites and ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Jia wrote New Discourses, and Tong fixed the rites and ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 此知變之善也。

translations.literal: This is the virtue of knowing when to change.
translations.idiomatic: This is the virtue of knowing when to change.

sentences.zh: 向若高帝斥二子，置《詩》、《書》，重攻戰，尊首級，則復道爭功，拔劍擊柱，晷漏之不保，何十二帝二百年乎？

translations.literal: Had the High Emperor rejected these two men, set aside the Poetry and Documents, stressed attack and battle, and honored taking heads, then again on the road to dispute merit, drawing swords to strike pillars — could a single day's time even be preserved? How then twelve emperors and two hundred years?
translations.idiomatic: Had the High Emperor rejected these two men, set aside the Poetry and Documents, stressed attack and battle, and honored taking heads, then again on the road to dispute merit, drawing swords to strike pillars — could a single day's time even be preserved? How then twelve emperors and two hundred years?

sentences.zh: 故曰：仁義者，聖人之蘧廬；

translations.literal: Hence it is said: Benevolence and righteousness are the sage's roadside inn;
translations.idiomatic: Hence it is said: Benevolence and righteousness are the sage's roadside inn;

sentences.zh: 禮者，先王之陳跡。

translations.literal: ritual is the former kings' trodden tracks.
translations.idiomatic: ritual is the former kings' trodden tracks.

sentences.zh: 祠祝畢，芻狗捐；

translations.literal: When the sacrifice is done, the straw dog is cast aside;
translations.idiomatic: When the sacrifice is done, the straw dog is cast aside;

sentences.zh: 淳精流，糟粕棄。

translations.literal: when the pure essence flows forth, the dregs are discarded.
translations.idiomatic: when the pure essence flows forth, the dregs are discarded.

sentences.zh: 仁義尚爾，況其輕乎？

translations.literal: If even benevolence and righteousness are thus, how much more what is lighter than them?
translations.idiomatic: If even benevolence and righteousness are thus, how much more what is lighter than them?

sentences.zh: 國家自文明以來，天地草昧，內則流言，外則構難。

translations.literal: Since the Wenming era our state has been in primal twilight — within, seditious talk; without, enemies fomenting trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wenming era our state has been in primal twilight — within, seditious talk; without, enemies fomenting trouble.

sentences.zh: 故不設鉤距，無以順人；

translations.literal: Therefore if one did not set traps and reckonings, there was no way to win men over;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore if one did not set traps and reckonings, there was no way to win men over;

sentences.zh: 不切刑罰，無以息暴。

translations.literal: if one did not apply severe punishments, there was no way to quell violence.
translations.idiomatic: if one did not apply severe punishments, there was no way to quell violence.

sentences.zh: 於是置神器，開告端，故能不出房闈，而天下晏然易主矣。

translations.literal: Thus the regalia of rule was set in place and the door of denunciation opened — and so, without leaving the inner chambers, the realm calmly changed masters.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the regalia of rule was set in place and the door of denunciation opened — and so, without leaving the inner chambers, the realm calmly changed masters.

sentences.zh: 臣聞急趨者無善跡，促柱者無和聲；

translations.literal: I have heard that one who runs in haste leaves no fine tracks, and one who tightens the pegs gets no harmonious sound;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that one who runs in haste leaves no fine tracks, and one who tightens the pegs gets no harmonious sound;

sentences.zh: 拯溺不規行，療饑不鼎食。

translations.literal: To save the drowning one does not keep to measured steps; to heal the starving one does not dine from a cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: To save the drowning one does not keep to measured steps; to heal the starving one does not dine from a cauldron.

sentences.zh: 即向時秘策，今之芻狗也。

translations.literal: The secret policies of that time are today's straw dogs.
translations.idiomatic: The secret policies of that time are today's straw dogs.

sentences.zh: 願鑒秦、漢之失，考時事之宜，毀蘧廬，遺糟粕；

translations.literal: I pray that Your Majesty reflect on the failures of Qin and Han, examine what the present age requires, tear down the roadside inns and leave behind the dregs;
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty reflect on the failures of Qin and Han, examine what the present age requires, tear down the roadside inns and leave behind the dregs;

sentences.zh: 下寬大之令，流曠蕩之澤，去萋斐之角牙，頓奸險之芒刃，塞羅織之妄源，掃朋黨之險跡，曠然使天下更始，豈不樂哉！

translations.literal: Issue orders of leniency and breadth, extend the bounty of magnanimous release, remove the fangs of malicious slander, blunt the razor edges of treachery, block the reckless springs of fabricated charges, sweep away the perilous traces of faction — openly giving the realm a new beginning. Would this not be joy itself!
translations.idiomatic: Issue orders of leniency and breadth, extend the bounty of magnanimous release, remove the fangs of malicious slander, blunt the razor edges of treachery, block the reckless springs of fabricated charges, sweep away the perilous traces of faction — openly giving the realm a new beginning. Would this not be joy itself!

sentences.zh: 后善其言。

translations.literal: The Empress approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress approved his words.

sentences.zh: 遷正諫大夫，兼修國史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Remonstrance Grand Master and concurrently charged with compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Remonstrance Grand Master and concurrently charged with compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 乃請高史官選，以求名才。

translations.literal: He thereupon requested elevating the selection of historiographers to seek men of renown and talent.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon requested elevating the selection of historiographers to seek men of renown and talent.

sentences.zh: 侍中韋安石嘗閱其稿史，歎曰：「董狐何以加！

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman Wei Anshi once reviewed his draft history and sighed: "What could Dong Hu add to this!
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gentleman Wei Anshi once reviewed his draft history and sighed: "What could Dong Hu add to this!

sentences.zh: 世人不知史官權重宰相，宰相但能制生人，史官兼制生死，古之聖君賢臣所以畏懼者也。」

translations.literal: The world does not know that the historian's authority outweighs the chief minister's — the chief minister can only command the living, but the historian commands both life and death. This is what made sage rulers and worthy ministers of old feel awe.
translations.idiomatic: The world does not know that the historian's authority outweighs the chief minister's — the chief minister can only command the living, but the historian commands both life and death. This is what made sage rulers and worthy ministers of old feel awe.

sentences.zh: 時賦斂繁重，民多蕩析，后數召入禁中訪失得，進同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: At the time levies were heavy and multitudinous; the people were much scattered and uprooted. The Empress repeatedly summoned him into the inner palace to inquire into gains and losses, and promoted him to Associate Director of the Fengge and Luantai Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the time levies were heavy and multitudinous; the people were much scattered and uprooted. The Empress repeatedly summoned him into the inner palace to inquire into gains and losses, and promoted him to Associate Director of the Fengge and Luantai Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 張易之構魏元忠、張説，欲誅之，無敢言者。

translations.literal: Zhang Yizhi framed Wei Yuanzhong and Zhang Yue, seeking to have them executed; no one dared speak out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yizhi framed Wei Yuanzhong and Zhang Yue, seeking to have them executed; no one dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 敬則獨奏曰：「元忠、説秉心忠一，而所坐無名，殺之失天下望。」

translations.literal: Jingze alone memorialized: "Yuanzhong and Yue bear faithful and single-minded hearts, yet the crimes charged against them have no substance — killing them would lose the hope of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze alone memorialized: "Yuanzhong and Yue bear faithful and single-minded hearts, yet the crimes charged against them have no substance — killing them would lose the hope of the realm.

sentences.zh: 乃得不死。

translations.literal: Thus they were not put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they were not put to death.

sentences.zh: 以老疾還政事，俄改成均祭酒、冬官侍郎。

translations.literal: Because of age and illness he returned his government duties; soon he was changed to Director of the Imperial University and Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Because of age and illness he returned his government duties; soon he was reassigned as Director of the Imperial University and Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 易之等集名儒撰《三教珠英》，又繪武三思、李嶠，蘇味道、李迥秀、王紹宗等十八人像以爲圖，欲引敬則，固辭不與，世潔其爲人。

translations.literal: Yizhi and his group gathered eminent scholars to compile Pearls of the Three Teachings, and also painted portraits of Wu Sansi, Li Jiao, Su Weidao, Li Huixiu, Wang Shaozong, and eighteen others altogether to make a pictorial scroll. They wished to include Jingze, but he firmly declined and would not join them; the world admired his character.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi and his group gathered eminent scholars to compile Pearls of the Three Teachings, and also painted portraits of Wu Sansi, Li Jiao, Su Weidao, Li Huixiu, Wang Shaozong, and eighteen others altogether to make a pictorial scroll. They wished to include Jingze, but he firmly declined; the world admired his character.

sentences.zh: 出爲鄭州刺史，遂致仕。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Zhengzhou and then retired.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as prefect of Zhengzhou and then retired.

sentences.zh: 侍御史冉祖雍誣奏與王同皎善，貶涪州刺史。

translations.literal: Censor Assistant Ran Zuyong falsely memorialized that he was close to Wang Tongjiao, and he was demoted to prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Assistant Ran Zuyong falsely memorialized that he was close to Wang Tongjiao, and he was demoted to prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 既明其非罪，改廬州。

translations.literal: Once his innocence was established, his post was changed to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once his innocence was established, his post was changed to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 代還，無淮南一物，所乘止一馬，子曹歩從以歸。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, he possessed not a single thing from Huainan; he rode only one horse, and his son Cao walked alongside him home.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he returned, he brought back not a single thing from Huainan; he rode only one horse, and his son Cao walked alongside him home.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十五。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at age seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 敬則與三從昆弟居四十年，貲產無異。

translations.literal: Jingze lived with three collateral cousins for forty years; their property and possessions were indistinguishable.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze lived with three collateral cousins for forty years; their property and possessions were held in common without distinction.

sentences.zh: 及執政，毎以用人爲先，細務不省也。

translations.literal: When he wielded power, he always put selecting personnel first and did not attend to petty affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When he wielded power, he always put selecting personnel first and did not attend to petty affairs.

sentences.zh: 嶺表蠻叛，以裴懷古有文武才，用爲桂州都督，蠻服其威惠，相率降。

translations.literal: When the barbarians of Lingnan rebelled, because Pei Huaigu possessed both civil and military talent, he was appointed military governor of Guizhou; the barbarians submitted to his authority and kindness and surrendered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians of Lingnan rebelled, because Pei Huaigu possessed both civil and military talent, Jingze appointed him military governor of Guizhou; the barbarians submitted to his authority and kindness and surrendered in succession.

sentences.zh: 薦魏知古爲鳳閣舍人，張思敬爲右史，皆稱職。

translations.literal: He recommended Wei Zhigu as Secretariat Attendant of the Fengge and Zhang Sijing as Right Historian — both proved competent in their posts.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Wei Zhigu as Secretariat Attendant of the Fengge and Zhang Sijing as Right Historian — both proved competent in their posts.

sentences.zh: 初，二張權寵盛，敬則密謂敬暉曰：「公若假太子令，舉北軍誅易之兄弟，兩飛騎力耳。」

translations.literal: Initially, when the Two Zhangs' power and favor were at their height, Jingze secretly told Jing Hui: "If you borrow the Crown Prince's command and mobilize the Northern Army to execute the Yizhi brothers, it would take but the strength of two Flying Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Two Zhangs' power and favor were at their height, Jingze secretly told Jing Hui: "If you borrow the Crown Prince's command and mobilize the Northern Army to execute the Yizhi brothers, it would take but the strength of two Flying Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 暉卒用其策。

translations.literal: In the end Hui adopted his stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Hui adopted his stratagem.

sentences.zh: 始崔實、仲長統、王朗、曹冏論封建，指秦爲失，敬則以爲秦、漢世禮義陵遲，不可復用周制封諸侯，著論明之，儒者以爲知言。

translations.literal: When Cui Shi, Zhongchang Tong, Wang Lang, and Cao Jiong debated enfeoffment and pointed to Qin as erring, Jingze held that in the Qin and Han eras ritual and righteousness had declined and one could not revive the Zhou system of enfeoffing feudal lords; he wrote a treatise to clarify this, and Confucian scholars deemed it perceptive speech.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Shi, Zhongchang Tong, Wang Lang, and Cao Jiong debated enfeoffment and pointed to Qin as erring, Jingze held that in the Qin and Han eras ritual and righteousness had declined and one could not revive the Zhou system of enfeoffing feudal lords; he wrote a treatise to clarify this, and Confucian scholars deemed it perceptive speech.

sentences.zh: 睿宗嗣位，嘗曰：「神龍以來，忠於本朝者，李多祚、王同晈、韋月將、燕欽融並褒復矣，尚有遺者耶？」

translations.literal: When Ruizong succeeded to the throne, he once said: "Since the Shenlong era, those loyal to our dynasty — Li Duozuo, Wang Tongjiao, Wei Yuejiang, and Yan Qinrong — have all been posthumously honored and restored. Are there still any overlooked?
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong succeeded to the throne, he once said: "Since the Shenlong era, those loyal to our dynasty — Li Duozuo, Wang Tongjiao, Wei Yuejiang, and Yan Qinrong — have all been posthumously honored and restored. Are there still any overlooked?

sentences.zh: 劉幽求曰：「硃敬則忠正義烈，天下所推，往爲宗楚客、冉祖雍等所誣，謫守刺史。

translations.literal: Liu Youqiu said: "Zhu Jingze was upright, loyal, and resolute — esteemed throughout the realm. Formerly he was slandered by Zong Chuke, Ran Zuyong, and others, and demoted to serve as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Youqiu said: "Zhu Jingze was upright, loyal, and resolute — esteemed throughout the realm. Formerly he was slandered by Zong Chuke, Ran Zuyong, and others, and demoted to serve as prefect.

sentences.zh: 長安中，嘗語臣曰：'相王必受命，當悉心事之。

translations.literal: In the Chang'an period he once told me: 'The Prince of Xiang will inevitably receive the Mandate — you must devote yourself wholly to serving him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chang'an period he once told me: 'The Prince of Xiang will inevitably receive the Mandate — you must devote yourself wholly to serving him.

sentences.zh: '及韋氏幹紀，臣遂見危赴難。

translations.literal: When the Wei clan committed outrage against the law, I thereupon saw the danger and went to meet the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei clan committed outrage against the law, I thereupon saw the danger and went to meet the crisis.

sentences.zh: 雖天誘其衷，亦敬則啟之。」

translations.literal: Though Heaven guided my heart, it was Jingze who opened the way.
translations.idiomatic: Though Heaven guided my heart, it was Jingze who opened the way.

sentences.zh: 於是追贈秘書監，諡曰元。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jingze was posthumously conferred as Director of the Palace Library, with the posthumous title Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Jingze was posthumously conferred as Director of the Palace Library, with the posthumous title Yuan.

sentences.zh: 敬則兄 仁軌敬則兄仁軌，字德容，隱居養親。

translations.literal: Jingze's elder brother Rengui, styled Derong, lived in seclusion to care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze's elder brother Rengui, whose courtesy name was Derong, lived in seclusion to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 常誨子弟曰：「終身讓路，不枉百歩；

translations.literal: He often admonished his children and younger relatives: "Yield the path all your life and you will not go a hundred paces out of your way;
translations.idiomatic: He often admonished his children and younger relatives: "Yield the path all your life and you will not go a hundred paces out of your way;

sentences.zh: 終身讓畔，不失一段。」

translations.literal: yield the boundary all your life and you will not lose a single plot.
translations.idiomatic: yield the boundary all your life and you will not lose a single plot.

sentences.zh: 有赤烏、白鵲棲所居樹，按察使趙承恩表其異。

translations.literal: Red crows and white magpies nested in the tree at his dwelling; the surveillance commissioner Zhao Chengen memorialized this as an auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: Red crows and white magpies nested in the tree at his dwelling; the surveillance commissioner Zhao Chengen memorialized this as an auspicious sign.

sentences.zh: 及卒，郭山惲、員半千、魏知古共諡爲孝友先生。

translations.literal: When he died, Guo Shanyun, Yuan Banqian, and Wei Zhigu jointly gave him the posthumous title Master of Filial Piety and Fraternity.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Guo Shanyun, Yuan Banqian, and Wei Zhigu jointly gave him the posthumous title Master of Filial Piety and Fraternity.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：武后乘唐中衰，操殺生柄，劫制天下而攘神器。

translations.literal: Commentary: Empress Wu seized upon the Tang's mid-dynasty decline, grasped the power of life and death, coerced the realm, and usurped the regalia of rule.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Empress Wu seized upon the Tang's mid-dynasty decline, grasped the power of life and death, coerced the realm, and usurped the regalia of rule.

sentences.zh: 仁傑蒙恥奮忠，以權大謀，引張柬之等，卒復唐室，功蓋一時，人不及知。

translations.literal: Renjie endured disgrace and roused loyalty, wielding great stratagem through borrowed authority; he led Zhang Jianzhi and others, and finally restored the house of Tang — his achievement eclipsed his age, though men did not fully know it.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie endured disgrace and roused loyalty, wielding great stratagem through borrowed authority; he led Zhang Jianzhi and others, and finally restored the house of Tang — his achievement eclipsed his age, though men did not fully know it.

sentences.zh: 故唐呂溫頌之曰：「取日虞淵，洗光咸池。

translations.literal: Hence Lü Wen of Tang praised him in verse: "Draw back the sun from the Pool of Darkness, rinse its light in the Pool of Universal Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Lü Wen of Tang praised him in verse: "Draw back the sun from the Pool of Darkness, rinse its light in the Pool of Universal Harmony.

sentences.zh: 潛授五龍，夾之以飛。」

translations.literal: Secretly invest the Five Dragons, flanking them with wings in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly invest the Five Dragons, flanking them with wings in flight.

sentences.zh: 世以爲名言。

translations.literal: The world took these lines for immortal words.
translations.idiomatic: The world took these lines for immortal words.

sentences.zh: 方高宗舉天下將以禪後，處俊固爭，不使妻乘夫，陰反陽，至奸人銜怨，仇胔以逞。

translations.literal: When Gaozong proposed to yield the realm to the Empress, Chujun firmly remonstrated — he would not let the wife ride over the husband, the yin overturn the yang — until wicked men nursed grievances and wreaked vengeance even upon the corpses of their enemies.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong proposed to yield the realm to the Empress, Chujun firmly remonstrated — he would not let the wife ride over the husband, the yin overturn the yang — until wicked men nursed grievances and wreaked vengeance even upon the corpses of their enemies.

sentences.zh: 蓋所謂誼形於主耶。

translations.literal: Was this not what is called righteousness taking visible form before the sovereign?
translations.idiomatic: Was this not what is called righteousness taking visible form before the sovereign?

sentences.zh: 敬則一諫，而羅織之獄衰，時而後言者歟！

translations.literal: With a single remonstrance Jingze brought the fabricated-charge trials to decline — was this not one who spoke at the right time!
translations.idiomatic: With a single remonstrance Jingze brought the fabricated-charge trials to decline — was this not one who spoke at the right time!
